question: Why is it important to maintain a space cushion between your vehicle and others?
options: a:It keeps traffic flowing at a faster pace.,b:It prevents distractions from other vehicles.,c:It allows you time to react to unexpected situations.
note: Maintaining a space cushion gives you extra time and room to react if another driver brakes suddenly, swerves, or makes a mistake. This buffer helps you avoid rear‑end collisions and sudden, unsafe maneuvers.

question: What is the 'No zone' around large trucks or buses?
options: a:A speed limit zone for trucks.,b:A restricted audio zone for loud stereos.,c:The vehicle’s blind spots where smaller vehicles may not be seen.
note: The “No zone” is the large blind spot area around trucks and buses where the driver cannot see you in their mirrors. Staying out of these areas—especially directly behind, directly in front, and along the sides near the cab—reduces the risk of being hit if the truck changes lanes or stops suddenly.

question: Why must you use extra caution when driving at night?
options: a:Because there is more traffic at night.,b:Because traffic moves faster at night.,c:Because drivers cannot see as well at night as during the day.
note: At night, your ability to see hazards, road signs, and pedestrians is reduced, and it is harder to judge distance and speed. Because visibility is limited, you must use extra caution, reduce speed as needed, and use your headlights from about half an hour after sunset to half an hour before sunrise or whenever you cannot see clearly ahead.

question: Is it ever acceptable to drive around or under a lowering or raising railroad crossing gate?
options: a:Only if your vehicle can do so without damaging the gate.,b:Only when there are no visible trains.,c:No — you must not drive around or under a gate that is moving.
note: Railroad gates, flashing lights, and bells mean a train is approaching or nearby, and you must stop. It is never safe or legal to drive around or under a lowering, lowered, or raising gate, even if you do not see a train, because trains can approach quickly and cannot stop in time.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: If another driver is passing you, what should you do?
options: a:Pull off the road.,b:Signal to tell them when to pass.,c:Maintain a steady speed or slightly adjust it so the passing vehicle can safely return to your lane.
note: When another driver is passing you, stay in your lane and do not speed up. If needed, slightly adjust your speed so the passing driver can safely move back into your lane with plenty of space. This reduces the time both vehicles are side‑by‑side and lowers the risk of a collision with oncoming traffic.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When should you use your turn signal?
options: a:Changing lanes.,b:Pulling into traffic from a parking area or alley.,c:Pulling into or out of a parking space.,d:All of the above.
note: Use your turn signal any time you intend to move left or right: when changing lanes, pulling into traffic from a curb, alley, or parking area, and when entering or leaving a parking space. Signaling lets other road users anticipate your movement and helps prevent collisions.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: Two solid white lines across a lane mark what area?
options: a:An area with no right-of-way rules.,b:A place where vehicles have right-of-way over pedestrians.,c:A crosswalk where pedestrians have the right-of-way.
note: Two solid white lines across the road mark a crosswalk. Drivers must yield to pedestrians who are in or entering the crosswalk, slowing or stopping as needed so they can cross safely.

question: Why must your vehicle be inspected at least once a year?
options: a:Only if it is older than five years old.,b:Unless it is a new vehicle.,c:To ensure it is safe to operate.
note: Annual safety inspections are required to make sure your vehicle is mechanically safe and in proper operating condition. Regular inspections help find problems like worn brakes, bad tires, or faulty lights before they cause a crash.

question: When roads are slippery, what driving adjustment should you make?
options: a:Reduce use of turn signals.,b:Drive as you would on dry roads.,c:Increase your following distance.
note: On slippery roads your tires have less traction, so it takes longer to stop. Increase your following distance so you have more space and time to brake gently and avoid skids or rear-end collisions.

question: If you must slow down on a slippery road, what is the first action you should take?
options: a:Take your foot off the gas pedal to reduce speed.,b:Firmly apply your brakes immediately.,c:Apply your parking brake.
note: On a slippery surface, the safest first step to slow down is to ease your foot off the accelerator and let the vehicle slow gradually. If you need to slow more, apply the brakes gently and steadily to avoid locking the wheels and losing control.

question: Compared to daytime driving, driving at night is:
options: a:No more or less dangerous.,b:Less dangerous.,c:More dangerous.
note: Driving at night is more dangerous because you cannot see as far ahead, it is harder to judge speed and distance, and glare from headlights can temporarily blind you. There are also more fatigued or impaired drivers on the road at night, so you must slow down and increase following distance.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: In which situations are you required to come to a stop?
options: a:Only at a stop sign.,b:Only when you see a flashing red light.,c:At a stop sign, at a steady or flashing red light, and whenever a traffic officer directs you to stop.
note: You are required to stop at more than just stop signs. You must come to a complete stop at stop signs, at steady or flashing red traffic lights, and whenever a traffic officer or flagger directs you to stop. You also must stop for school buses with flashing red lights (when required by state law) and at railroad crossings when signals or gates indicate a train is coming.

question: How should you avoid collisions due to blind spots?
options: a:Adjust rearview mirrors every few minutes.,b:Honk just before turning or changing lanes.,c:Quickly glance over your shoulder to check the blind spot before changing lanes.
note: Every vehicle has blind spots that mirrors cannot show. Before changing lanes or merging, quickly turn your head and glance over your shoulder in the direction you plan to move to check these blind spots. Do not rely only on mirrors, and do not use your horn as a substitute for checking.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: What does a flashing red traffic light mean?
options: a:The traffic signal is broken.,b:The same thing as a stop sign.,c:You do not have to come to a complete stop.
note: A flashing red light is treated the same as a stop sign. You must come to a complete stop, yield to pedestrians and other traffic in or close to the intersection, and proceed only when it is safe.

question: Which statements about railroad crossings are true?
options: a:You may drive around lowered gates if no train is visible.,b:All of the following: It is against the law to go around lowered gates; you must stop when directed by a flagger; not all crossings have flashing lights and gates.,c:Only that all crossings have flashing red signals and gates.
note: At railroad crossings, it is illegal and extremely dangerous to drive around lowered gates, even if you do not see a train. You must obey flaggers and all warning devices. Not all crossings have flashing lights or gates, so you must always look and listen for trains and be prepared to stop.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: A flashing red traffic signal at an intersection requires the same action as which device?
options: a:A slow sign.,b:A yield sign.,c:A stop sign.
note: A flashing red light means you must come to a complete stop, just as you would at a stop sign. After stopping, yield to any traffic or pedestrians with the right‑of‑way, then proceed when it is safe.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: What should you do before making a turn?
options: a:Increase your speed.,b:Turn the wheel without signaling.,c:Use your signal.
note: Before making any turn, you must signal to let other drivers, cyclists, and pedestrians know what you intend to do. Turn on your signal well in advance—typically at least 100 feet before the turn in most areas—so others have time to react safely.

question: Which action best describes a good defensive driver?
options: a:Travels at a constant speed at all times.,b:Looks out for the actions of other drivers and anticipates problems.,c:Drives slowly at all times.
note: A good defensive driver constantly scans the road, watches what other drivers are doing, and anticipates possible problems. They adjust speed and position to avoid hazards instead of assuming others will always follow the rules.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: If a flagger is directing traffic in a work zone, what must you do?
options: a:Follow the directions given by the flagger.,b:Ignore the flagger and follow surrounding traffic.,c:Assume the flagger does not apply to you.
note: In work zones, flaggers have the legal authority to direct traffic. You must follow their signals and instructions, even if traffic lights or signs indicate something different, because they are managing temporary and changing hazards.

question: If you are taking a non-prescription (over-the-counter) drug, what should you do before driving?
options: a:Drink alcohol instead.,b:Read the labels on the drug and heed any warnings about driving.,c:Continue to drive regardless of any warning labels.
note: Many over‑the‑counter medicines can cause drowsiness, slow reaction time, or affect judgment. Always read the label and follow any warnings about driving or operating machinery, and avoid driving if the medication may impair you.

question: Your blind spot is the area of the road that:
options: a:You cannot see without moving your head.,b:Is directly behind your vehicle.,c:You see in your rearview mirror.
note: A blind spot is any area you cannot see with your mirrors alone and must turn your head to check. These areas are typically to the sides and slightly behind your vehicle, outside the view of your rearview and side mirrors.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When making a left turn at a green traffic light, you must:
options: a:Always have the right-of-way.,b:Yield to oncoming traffic before completing the left turn.,c:Always drive straight through the intersection.
note: On a green light, you may turn left only after yielding to oncoming traffic and pedestrians. Wait until there is a safe gap, then complete your turn without forcing others to slow or stop suddenly.

question: When backing a vehicle, what should you do?
options: a:Open the door to check behind you.,b:Rely only on your mirrors.,c:Turn your head and look through the rear window; do not rely solely on mirrors.
note: When backing, turn your head and look directly through the rear window so you can clearly see behind you. Use your mirrors only as a supplement; they can miss children, pedestrians, and low objects close to your vehicle.

question: What is a reliable strategy to avoid driving while impaired after social drinking?
options: a:Take a cold shower to sober up quickly.,b:Arrange a ride home with a friend who has not been drinking.,c:Drink coffee before driving.
note: The only safe strategy is to avoid driving after drinking at all. Arrange a sober ride—such as a designated driver, taxi, or rideshare—because coffee, showers, or other tricks do not reduce your blood alcohol level.

question: If your vehicle begins to skid, how should you turn the steering wheel?
options: a:In the opposite direction of the skid.,b:In the direction you want the vehicle to go.,c:To keep the front wheels straight.
note: If your vehicle starts to skid, ease off the accelerator and steer in the direction you want the front of the vehicle to go. As the tires regain traction, continue steering smoothly to keep control and avoid overcorrecting.

question: When crossing railroad tracks, what should you do to be safe?
options: a:Listen,b:Look and listen for trains in both directions and only cross when it is clearly safe.,c:Cross especially quickly when a train is approaching.
note: At railroad crossings, you must slow down, look carefully in both directions, and listen for trains. Only cross the tracks when you are sure no train is coming and there is enough space to clear the tracks completely. Never try to cross quickly when a train is approaching; trains are much faster and need far more distance to stop than a car.

question: After an accident, what is one of the first actions you should take?
options: a:Stop your vehicle at or near the scene.,b:Avoid standing or walking in traffic lanes after you have safely stopped.,c:When safe, turn off the ignition of any wrecked vehicles.
note: After a crash, the law requires you to stop your vehicle at or as close as possible to the scene without blocking traffic more than necessary. Once stopped, you should check for injuries, avoid standing in traffic lanes, and, when safe, turn off the ignitions of wrecked vehicles to reduce fire risk.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When making a right turn on a steady green light, what must you do?
options: a:Maintain your normal driving speed through the turn.,b:Stop and look only for police cars.,c:Yield to pedestrians and other vehicles before turning.
note: On a steady green light, you may make a right turn if it is not prohibited by a sign, but you must first yield to pedestrians in the crosswalk and to any vehicles already in or close to the intersection. Slow down, scan for people crossing and oncoming traffic, and complete the turn only when the way is clear.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When is it permissible to pass another vehicle?
options: a:By using the shoulder of the highway.,b:In a curve or on a hill where visibility is limited.,c:Only when your lane is next to a broken yellow or white line and it is safe to pass.
note: You may pass another vehicle only where passing is allowed by pavement markings (such as a broken yellow center line) and only when you have enough clear distance ahead to pass safely. Never pass on the shoulder, on a hill, or in a curve where your view of oncoming traffic is limited.

question: Which statement about seat belts and child restraints is true?
options: a:You should always make sure all your passengers are using a seat belt or child restraint.,b:You should never place a rear-facing infant in the front seat of a vehicle with an active passenger airbag.,c:An airbag can be dangerous to an infant or small child, especially in a low-speed collision.
note: Drivers are responsible for making sure every passenger is properly restrained with a seat belt or an appropriate child safety seat. Airbags can seriously injure infants and small children, especially those in rear‑facing seats, so they should ride in the back seat whenever possible and always in the correct child restraint for their size and age.

question: What do your brake lights communicate to drivers behind you?
options: a:That your emergency brake is engaged.,b:That you are slowing down or stopping.,c:That you are making a turn.
note: Brake lights warn drivers behind you that you are slowing down or stopping so they can react in time and avoid a rear-end collision. Always keep your brake lights clean and in good working order.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: If you are driving in the left lane and plan to move into the right lane, what should you do first?
options: a:Check your mirrors first, then signal and check your blind spot before moving.,b:Signal only if you see a vehicle directly beside you.,c:Move into the lane first, then check your mirrors.
note: Before changing lanes, you must first check your mirrors to see traffic behind and beside you. Then signal, and finally check your blind spot by looking over your shoulder before moving into the lane.

question: What is the effect of taking drugs with alcohol before driving?
options: a:It reduces the alcohol's effects.,b:It is no more dangerous than alcohol alone.,c:It increases the risk of causing a crash by amplifying impairment.
note: Combining alcohol with drugs—whether prescription, over-the-counter, or illegal—can greatly increase drowsiness, slow reaction time, and impair judgment more than either substance alone, making a crash much more likely.

question: What is the purpose of regulatory signs?
options: a:To mark scenic routes.,b:To indicate actions drivers must or must not take in a designated area.,c:To mark areas of public recreation.
note: Regulatory signs tell you what you must do or must not do in that area, such as speed limits, lane use, turns, parking, and other rules you are legally required to follow.

question: If your power steering fails while driving, what should you do?
options: a:Turn on your hazard lights and immediately shut off the engine while still in traffic.,b:Steer with extra effort, slow down, and move carefully to a safe place off the road.,c:Honk continuously and continue driving to the nearest service station.
note: If power steering fails, the vehicle will still steer, but it will take much more effort. Keep a firm grip on the wheel, slow down, and carefully steer to the side of the road where you can stop safely and get the vehicle checked.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: If you miss your freeway exit, what is the correct action?
options: a:Go to the next exit.,b:Make a U-turn through the median.,c:Pull onto the shoulder and back your car to the exit.
note: If you miss your freeway exit, you must continue to the next exit and then re-route from there. Never stop on the freeway, back up on the shoulder, or make a U-turn through the median, as these maneuvers are extremely dangerous and illegal on most freeways.

question: When entering a street from a garage or alley, what must a driver do?
options: a:Yield to other drivers and pedestrians.,b:Assume you have the right-of-way.,c:Drive quickly to merge into traffic.
note: When entering a street from a driveway, garage, or alley, you must stop if necessary and yield to all pedestrians and vehicles already on the roadway. Traffic on the public street has the right-of-way, so only enter when it is safe.

question: Why is a leaky exhaust system dangerous?
options: a:Because it causes a loss of hearing.,b:Because it can allow carbon monoxide to enter the passenger compartment and poison occupants.,c:Because it only increases pollution with no other effects.
note: A leaky exhaust system is dangerous because it can allow carbon monoxide, a colorless and odorless poisonous gas, to enter the passenger compartment. Breathing carbon monoxide can quickly cause illness, unconsciousness, or death, so exhaust leaks must be repaired immediately.

question: What does a solid red arrow on a traffic signal mean?
options: a:You may turn with caution.,b:The arrow is not used as a traffic signal.,c:The same as a circular red — stop and do not turn in the arrow’s direction.
note: A solid red arrow means you must stop and remain stopped if you are in the lane controlled by that arrow. You may not turn in the direction of the arrow until it changes to green or a permitted signal, and only then proceed when it is safe.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: If two vehicles arrive at an intersection at the same time without signs or signals, which vehicle has the right-of-way?
options: a:The vehicle whose driver sounds a horn first.,b:The vehicle approaching from the left.,c:The vehicle approaching from the right.
note: At an uncontrolled intersection where two vehicles arrive at the same time, the driver must yield to the vehicle on their right. This rule helps determine right-of-way when there are no signs, signals, or other controls present.

question: Which factors greatly affect your ability to stop a vehicle?
options: a:Road surface and weather conditions (e.g., wet, icy, gravel),b:Only the signal lights at an intersection,c:The time of day you are driving.
note: Stopping distance depends heavily on road surface, weather, tire condition, and speed. Wet, icy, or loose surfaces like gravel reduce traction and increase the distance it takes to stop, even if you brake properly.

question: What color pavement markings separate traffic moving in opposite directions?
options: a:White,b:Blue,c:Yellow
note: In the U.S., yellow pavement markings separate traffic moving in opposite directions, usually as center lines. White lines separate lanes of traffic moving in the same direction, and blue is used for things like accessible parking, not lane separation.

question: Before backing out of a driveway where children are playing, what should you do?
options: a:Start the car and back out slowly while watching your mirrors.,b:Sound the horn to warn the children.,c:Get out and walk to the back of the car to be sure the way is clear.
note: Before backing where children may be present, you should walk behind the vehicle and check the area. Mirrors and cameras have blind spots close to the vehicle, so physically checking behind you is the safest way to avoid hitting a child or object.

question: When should you signal when passing another vehicle?
options: a:After changing lanes.,b:Just before changing lanes.,c:Early enough for other drivers to know your plans in advance.
note: You must signal well before you change lanes or pass so other drivers have time to see and react to your intentions. Turn on your signal several seconds in advance, check mirrors and blind spots, then move only when it is safe.

question: When you hear a siren or see flashing lights of an approaching emergency vehicle, what must you do?
options: a:Motion for the emergency vehicle to pass you.,b:Stop your vehicle immediately and prevent them from passing.,c:Drive to the right side of the road and stop until it passes.
note: When an emergency vehicle approaches with lights or siren on, you must yield the right-of-way by safely moving to the right side of the road and stopping until it has passed. Never block or race an emergency vehicle, and do not stop in a way that prevents it from getting through.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: If you reach an intersection and need to turn but are in the wrong lane, what should you do?
options: a:Quickly cut across traffic to complete the turn.,b:Signal and make the turn from your current lane.,c:Drive to the next intersection and make the turn from the correct lane.
note: If you are in the wrong lane for a turn when you reach an intersection, continue straight and go to the next intersection where you can get into the correct lane. Sudden lane changes or cutting across traffic are dangerous and can cause crashes.

question: On a vertically arranged traffic signal, what is the top-to-bottom order of lights?
options: a:Green on top, yellow in the middle, red on the bottom.,b:Red on top, yellow in the middle, green on the bottom.,c:Red on top, green in the middle, yellow on the bottom.
note: On a standard vertical traffic signal in the U.S., the red light is always at the top, yellow in the middle, and green at the bottom. Drivers rely on this consistent order so they can understand the signal even in poor visibility or if colors are hard to distinguish.

question: If your vehicle's accelerator becomes stuck open, what action should you take?
options: a:Slam on the brakes immediately without changing gears.,b:Turn on your four‑way flashers and continue driving.,c:Shift to neutral, steer to a safe place, and then turn off the ignition carefully (avoiding locking the steering).
note: If the accelerator sticks, shift to neutral, keep a firm grip on the wheel, and steer to a safe place off the road. Then turn the ignition off only far enough to stop the engine so you do not lock the steering. Braking while in neutral helps you slow and stop under control.

question: When is it permissible to cross double solid yellow lines?
options: a:To pass another car.,b:To pass a slow-moving truck.,c:To turn into or out of a driveway or to make a permitted left turn.
note: Double solid yellow lines mean traffic in both directions is prohibited from passing. However, you may carefully cross them to turn left into or out of a driveway, side road, or alley, or to make another permitted left turn when it is safe.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: Which condition must be met before attempting to pass on a two-way, two-lane road?
options: a:All of the above — you must be able to see ahead, return to your lane before meeting oncoming traffic, and have sufficient speed.,b:You must be able to return to your lane before meeting oncoming traffic.,c:Your vehicle must be capable of the speed necessary to complete the pass.,d:You must be able to clearly see the road ahead far enough to pass safely.
note: Before passing on a two-way, two-lane road, you must be sure you can clearly see far enough ahead, your vehicle can accelerate fast enough to pass, and you can return to your lane before meeting oncoming traffic. If any of these conditions are not met, you must not pass.

question: What do crossbuck signs indicate?
options: a:A no-passing zone.,b:A school zone is ahead.,c:A railroad crossing is ahead.
note: Crossbuck signs are white X-shaped signs placed at railroad crossings. They indicate that you are at a railroad crossing and must yield to any approaching train, stopping if necessary. Trains always have the right-of-way.

question: When a police officer stops you for a traffic violation or equipment inspection, what documents must you present?
options: a:Only the vehicle registration.,b:License, registration, and proof of insurance.,c:Only proof of insurance.
note: When an officer stops you, you must be able to show your driver license, the vehicle registration, and proof of insurance. All three are required documents for legal driving and vehicle operation on public roads.

question: To prepare for hazards ahead, what driving technique should you use?
options: a:Stare straight ahead at all times.,b:Continually scan the entire road and all roadsides.,c:Drive with your left foot resting lightly on the brake pedal.
note: To spot hazards early, you should continually scan the entire road and the roadsides, checking ahead, to the sides, and using your mirrors. Avoid staring at one spot and never rest your foot on the brake pedal, which can cause unnecessary wear and confuse drivers behind you.

question: What should small-vehicle drivers be ready for when passing a large vehicle?
options: a:Loud engine noises only.,b:Extra air pollution but no steering effects.,c:Wind gusts that can shift your vehicle's direction.
note: When passing large vehicles such as trucks or buses, be prepared for strong wind gusts and air turbulence that can push or pull your vehicle sideways. Keep a firm grip on the steering wheel and allow extra space when passing.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When turning onto a street that has multiple lanes going your direction, into which lane should you turn?
options: a:Turn into the lane closest to the lane you are coming from.,b:Turn into the middle lane.,c:Turn into any lane you prefer as long as it is going your direction.
note: When turning onto a street with multiple lanes going your direction, you must turn into the lane that is closest to the lane you are coming from. Complete the turn first, then change lanes if needed when it is safe and legal to do so.

question: What does a round traffic sign usually warn you about?
options: a:A no-passing zone.,b:A school zone.,c:An upcoming railroad crossing.
note: Round (circular) warning signs in the U.S. are used specifically to warn of an upcoming railroad crossing. When you see this sign, slow down, look and listen for trains, and be prepared to stop if necessary.

question: Before passing another vehicle, what should you check?
options: a:Your mirrors and blind spots, and signal before changing lanes.,b:Honk to alert the driver to move over.,c:That you can re-enter within 10 feet of the passed vehicle.
note: Before passing, check your mirrors and blind spots to be sure the lane is clear, then signal and move over safely. After passing, only move back when you can see the entire front of the passed vehicle in your rearview mirror—do not rely on a fixed distance like 10 feet.

question: On average, the human body eliminates alcohol at about what rate?
options: a:Three alcoholic drinks per hour.,b:One standard alcoholic drink per hour.,c:Two alcoholic drinks per hour.
note: A common guideline is that the body processes about one standard drink per hour, but this varies widely by person, body size, food intake, and other factors. Because you can still be impaired even at low levels, you should never rely on this rate to decide if it is safe to drive.

question: Under what circumstances may you drive around railroad crossing gates?
options: a:If the train has just passed and the gate is still lowering.,b:Under no circumstances.,c:When the lights have stopped flashing and the train is gone.
note: You must never drive around, under, or through lowered or lowering railroad gates. Wait until the train has passed, the lights and bells stop, and the gates are fully raised before proceeding.

question: Which statement about sudden weather changes is correct?
options: a:You should watch both vehicles ahead of you and behind you.,b:You should slow down and increase following distance in rain or fog.,c:All of the above.
note: When weather changes suddenly, you must adjust your driving. Slow down in rain, fog, snow, or ice; increase your following distance; and watch both vehicles ahead of you and behind you, since stopping distances increase and visibility may be reduced.

question: What does a flashing yellow traffic light indicate?
options: a:Stop and wait for a green light.,b:Speed up to clear the intersection.,c:Slow down and proceed with caution.
note: A flashing yellow light means you do not have to stop, but you must slow down, look carefully in all directions, and proceed through the intersection only when it is safe.

question: When may you drive across a dashed white line?
options: a:When it is safe to change lanes.,b:Only during daylight hours.,c:At any time even if unsafe.
note: A dashed white line separates lanes moving in the same direction. You may cross it to change lanes or pass, but only when you have checked traffic and it is safe to do so.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When changing lanes on a highway, you should:
options: a:Signal a lane change.,b:Check your blind spot by glancing over your shoulder.,c:Check your rearview and outside mirrors.,d:All of the above — signal, check mirrors, and check your blind spot.
note: Before changing lanes, always signal, check your mirrors to see traffic behind and beside you, and quickly glance over your shoulder to check your blind spot where mirrors cannot see.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: A sign reading 'Reduced speed, 35 mph' indicates what?
options: a:The new 35 mph speed limit begins at the next posted speed limit sign.,b:That you have plenty of time to slow before the reduced zone.,c:The new 35 mph speed limit begins at this sign.
note: An advance "Reduced speed ahead" sign warns that a lower speed limit is coming up so you can begin slowing down. The new speed limit does not take effect until you reach the actual speed limit sign showing that lower number.

question: Which of these is not a safe action when passing another road user?
options: a:Leaving less than four feet of space between your vehicle and the vehicle you are overtaking.,b:Allowing a bicyclist extra room when passing them on the roadway.,c:Signaling to let other drivers know you will change lanes.
note: When passing, you must leave a safe clearance from the vehicle or bicyclist you are overtaking—many states require at least three or four feet for bicycles. You should always signal lane changes and give extra room to vulnerable road users, so crowding them with less than four feet of space is unsafe.

question: Is it legal to drink alcoholic beverages in a vehicle on a public road?
options: a:Yes if you are a passenger in the back seat.,b:No — consuming or possessing open alcohol on public roads is illegal.,c:Yes if you are in the bed of a pickup truck.
note: Open container laws in most U.S. jurisdictions make it illegal to drink alcohol or have an open alcoholic beverage in a vehicle on a public road, whether you are the driver or a passenger. Any open container in an area accessible to the driver or passengers is generally prohibited.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: Which of the following statements about speed is true?
options: a:Driving too slowly on certain highways can be dangerous.,b:Speeding can kill.,c:Speeding is not dangerous if you are a skilled driver.
note: Driving too slowly can be dangerous because it disrupts the normal flow of traffic and can cause sudden braking, lane changes, and rear-end collisions. Speeding is always dangerous, regardless of driver skill, because higher speeds increase stopping distance, crash risk, and crash severity.

question: How is distracted driving best described?
options: a:Nothing to be concerned about.,b:A rare occurrence.,c:Extremely risky behavior that endangers everyone on the road.
note: Distracted driving is extremely risky because it takes your eyes, mind, or hands away from the driving task. Even a brief distraction, such as looking at a phone or adjusting controls, can greatly increase the chance of a crash and endanger everyone on the road.

question: Which practices can help reduce road rage and aggressive driving?
options: a:Obeying posted speed limits.,b:Allowing extra travel time.,c:Using proper turn signals.,d:All of the above.
note: Allowing extra travel time helps you stay calm and avoid feeling rushed, which reduces the likelihood of aggressive driving and road rage. Obeying speed limits and using proper turn signals also help prevent conflicts with other drivers, but all of these practices together are most effective.

question: If you are in the right lane and want to move into the left lane on a multilane highway, what should you do?
options: a:Just check your rearview mirror and move over slowly.,b:Turn on your hazard lights and move left.,c:Look over your left shoulder to check your blind spot and signal before changing lanes.
note: Before changing lanes, always check your mirrors and then look over your shoulder toward the lane you want to enter to check your blind spot. Signal before you move so other drivers know your intentions, and change lanes only when it is safe.

question: Which of these items can be a distraction while driving?
options: a:Food and beverages.,b:Pets moving around inside the vehicle.,c:CD players
note: Anything that takes your eyes, hands, or mind away from driving is a distraction. Eating or drinking, handling pets, and using audio devices or other electronics can all increase your crash risk. You should avoid or minimize these activities while the vehicle is moving.

question: What should be your first response to reduced visibility?
options: a:Reduce your speed.,b:Turn on windshield wipers only.,c:Turn on interior lights.
note: When visibility decreases due to fog, heavy rain, darkness, or other conditions, your first response should be to slow down. Reducing speed gives you more time to see hazards and react safely. You may also need to use headlights and wipers as conditions require.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: If the line dividing your lane from the lane you wish to enter is what type of line may you pass?
options: a:Double solid yellow.,b:Solid yellow.,c:Broken white.
note: Broken white lines separate lanes of traffic moving in the same direction. You may cross a broken white line to change lanes or pass when it is safe. Solid yellow or double solid yellow lines generally mean you may not pass or cross except when turning or as specifically allowed.

question: Which of the following can impair your ability to drive?
options: a:All of the following: alcohol, medications, and lack of sleep.,b:Only alcohol.,c:Only lack of sleep.
note: Alcohol, many prescription or over‑the‑counter medications, illegal drugs, and being very tired or drowsy can all slow your reactions and impair judgment. Any of these can make driving unsafe, so you must be alert to how they affect you before getting behind the wheel.

question: How should you behave when you see a blind pedestrian using a white cane or guide dog?
options: a:Proceed normally at the same speed.,b:Slow down and be prepared to stop.,c:Take the right-of-way.
note: Blind pedestrians using a white cane or guide dog have the right‑of‑way. You must slow down, be prepared to stop, and yield so they can cross safely. Never insist on your right‑of‑way or drive close to them, as they rely on sound and predictable driver behavior.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: Which of the following locations is passing prohibited?
options: a:At all times on two-lane roads.,b:Only when following large trucks.,c:On hills and curves.
note: Passing is especially dangerous and usually illegal where you cannot clearly see oncoming traffic, such as on hills and curves, near intersections, and at railroad crossings. Limited visibility means you may not have enough distance to safely complete a pass before meeting oncoming vehicles.

question: When an emergency vehicle is displaying flashing red or blue lights and approaching, what must you do?
options: a:See if you can reach your destination before it catches up to you.,b:Pull over to the side of the road and come to a complete stop.,c:Continue driving but try to stay out of its way.
note: When an emergency vehicle with flashing red or blue lights and/or a siren approaches, you must immediately yield the right‑of‑way by pulling as far to the right side of the road as safely possible and coming to a complete stop. Remain stopped until the emergency vehicle has passed, unless a police officer directs otherwise. This creates a clear path so they can respond quickly and safely.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: Before making a left turn, it is important to:
options: a:Swing to the right side of your lane before turning.,b:Sound your horn to warn others.,c:Yield to oncoming vehicles and pedestrians.
note: Before making a left turn, you must yield the right‑of‑way to oncoming vehicles and pedestrians in the crosswalk. Wait until there is a safe gap in traffic and the path is clear, then turn into the correct lane without swinging wide or using your horn as a substitute for yielding.

question: Which of the following is NOT a factor in determining stopping distance?
options: a:Reaction distance,b:Braking distance,c:Steering ability
note: Stopping distance is the total distance your vehicle travels from the moment you see a hazard until you come to a complete stop. It includes perception time (seeing and recognizing the hazard), reaction distance (how far you travel while moving your foot to the brake), and braking distance (how far you travel while braking). Steering ability does not directly determine how far it takes you to stop.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: At a stop sign in a line of vehicles, if there is no cross traffic after vehicles ahead have cleared, what must you do?
options: a:Slowly roll past the stop sign without stopping.,b:Stop again at the stop sign or stop line before proceeding.,c:Proceed without stopping since others already did.
note: At a stop sign, each driver must come to a complete stop at the stop line, crosswalk, or before entering the intersection, even if vehicles ahead have already stopped and gone. After stopping, you must yield to any cross traffic or pedestrians before proceeding.

question: If you are driving in another vehicle's blind spot, what is the correct action?
options: a:Stay in the blind spot to prevent lane changes.,b:Move forward or drop back so the other driver can see you.,c:Maintain your position and speed.
note: Staying in another vehicle’s blind spot is dangerous because the driver cannot see you and may change lanes into your path. Either move ahead so you are clearly visible in their mirrors or drop back so you can see their mirrors and they can see you.

question: What most often causes motor vehicle crashes?
options: a:Poor road conditions.,b:Actions or errors on the part of the driver.,c:Large trucks.
note: Most crashes are caused by driver actions or errors such as speeding, distraction, following too closely, or failing to yield. While road conditions and vehicle type can contribute, safe and attentive driving is the primary factor in preventing most collisions.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When preparing for a right turn, where should your vehicle be positioned?
options: a:Near the center of the street.,b:Close to the left side of the street.,c:As close to the right side of the road as possible.
note: Before making a right turn, you should be in the rightmost lane and position your vehicle as close to the right curb or edge of the roadway as is safe. This helps prevent other vehicles, bicycles, or pedestrians from getting between you and the curb during the turn.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: Is it permissible to stop in a travel lane to look up an address or drop off passengers?
options: a:Yes — you may stop to drop off passengers.,b:No — you should not stop in a travel lane; pull off the road to a safe place.,c:Yes — you may stop to look up an address.
note: You must keep travel lanes clear. Do not stop in a lane of moving traffic to look for an address or to pick up or drop off passengers. Instead, continue until you can safely pull out of the traffic lane, such as into a parking area or designated curb zone.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: A steady red traffic signal requires you to:
options: a:Stop before entering the intersection.,b:Stop at the stop line.,c:Stop before entering any crosswalk.
note: At a steady red light, you must come to a complete stop at the stop line. If there is no stop line, stop before entering the crosswalk. If there is no crosswalk, stop before entering the intersection. Always stop where you can clearly see cross traffic and pedestrians.

question: Signs that warn you of hazardous conditions are called:
options: a:Warning signs.,b:Regulatory signs.,c:Information signs.
note: Warning signs are used to alert drivers to potential hazards or changes in road conditions ahead, such as curves, intersections, or pedestrian crossings. They give you time to slow down or adjust your driving to avoid danger.

question: Which factor does vehicle stopping distance not depend on?
options: a:The condition of your vehicle's brakes.,b:Your own reaction time.,c:The time of day.
note: Total stopping distance is the distance your vehicle travels from the moment you see a hazard until you come to a complete stop. It depends on your reaction time, the condition of your brakes and tires, road surface, and speed. The time of day by itself is not a direct factor, even though conditions that often change with time of day (like visibility) can affect how quickly you react.

question: When approaching a flashing red traffic light, drivers should:
options: a:Drive through the intersection if there is no crossing traffic.,b:Come to a complete stop.,c:Continue driving because they have the right-of-way.
note: A flashing red traffic light must be treated like a stop sign. You are required to come to a complete stop at the stop line, crosswalk, or before entering the intersection, then yield to other traffic and pedestrians and proceed only when it is safe.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: At an intersection, when must you stop for a traffic signal?
options: a:For a steady yellow light.,b:For a flashing red light.,c:For a yellow arrow.
note: You must stop at a flashing red signal just as you would at a stop sign: stop completely, check for traffic and pedestrians, yield as required, and proceed only when safe. A steady yellow or yellow arrow is a warning that the light is about to turn red; you should stop if you can do so safely, but they are not always an absolute stop requirement the way a flashing red is.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: If you are driving so slowly that traffic is backing up behind you on a two-lane, two-way road, what must you do?
options: a:Decrease your speed further.,b:Pull off the right side of the road and let traffic pass.,c:Not let the other cars pass your vehicle.
note: If you are driving so slowly that traffic is building up behind you on a two-lane, two-way road, you are required to pull off the road at a safe place when possible and let the vehicles behind you pass. This helps prevent unsafe passing and reduces the risk of rear-end or head-on collisions.

question: To relieve fatigue on a long trip, what is a good practice?
options: a:Drive with one eye open at a time.,b:Do arm exercises every hour.,c:Stop and rest every two hours.
note: Stopping to rest about every two hours is a recommended way to reduce fatigue on long trips. Getting out of the car, stretching, and even taking a short nap if you feel drowsy helps keep you alert and safe. You should never try tricks like driving with one eye closed; if you feel tired, you must stop driving.

question: Which practice helps prevent crashes by making your intentions clear to others?
options: a:Drive only on side streets to avoid traffic.,b:Ignore other drivers on the road.,c:Communicate with other road users by signaling and using appropriate warnings.
note: Crashes are less likely when other road users can predict what you are going to do. Using your turn signals, brake lights, horn (when needed), and appropriate hand signals clearly communicates your intentions so others can adjust their driving and avoid conflicts.

question: Does the type of alcoholic beverage change how alcohol affects your judgment and reflexes?
options: a:Yes — beer has much less effect than wine.,b:Yes — hard ciders affect you most.,c:No — any alcoholic beverage can impair reflexes and judgment depending on amount.
note: Any drink containing alcohol can impair your judgment, coordination, and reflexes. The key factor is how much alcohol you consume, not whether it comes from beer, wine, or liquor. A standard serving of each has roughly the same amount of alcohol and can affect you similarly.

question: Which factors affect braking distance?
options: a:The radio volume.,b:Vehicle speed.,c:Color of the vehicle.
note: Braking distance is the distance your vehicle travels after you apply the brakes until it stops. The faster you are going, the longer it takes to stop, so speed is a major factor. Braking distance is also affected by the condition of your brakes and tires and by the road surface, but not by things like radio volume or vehicle color.

question: How can you avoid the risks of alcohol-related crashes?
options: a:Drink slowly to avoid impairment.,b:Decide before you start drinking that you will not drive.,c:Say 'No thanks.'
note: The safest way to avoid an alcohol‑related crash is to decide in advance that you will not drive after drinking and to arrange a safe way home, such as a designated driver, taxi, or rideshare. Once you start drinking, your judgment is already affected, so planning ahead is critical.

question: A person walking with a white cane or guide dog is most likely to be:
options: a:Deaf.,b:Participating in a traffic study.,c:A person who is blind or visually impaired.
note: A white cane or guide dog identifies a pedestrian who is blind or visually impaired. Drivers must always yield the right‑of‑way, be prepared to stop well in advance, and avoid honking or revving the engine, which can confuse or frighten the person.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: If you miss your exit on a freeway, what is the proper action?
options: a:Make the turn quickly from your lane of travel.,b:Continue driving until the next exit.,c:Stop and back up.
note: If you miss your exit on a freeway, stay calm, keep going, and take the next exit. Never stop, back up, or make a sudden turn across lanes on the freeway, because traffic is moving at high speed and those actions can easily cause a serious crash.

question: What are the usual colors for warning signs about upcoming hazards?
options: a:White on blue.,b:Black symbols or letters on a yellow background.,c:Black on white.
note: Most general warning signs are yellow with black symbols or letters. They alert you to curves, intersections, pedestrian crossings, and other hazards ahead so you can slow down and be prepared. Work zone warning signs are usually orange with black symbols or letters.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: How should you respond to a flashing yellow traffic light?
options: a:Turn on your headlights.,b:Slow down and proceed with caution.,c:Come to a complete stop.
note: A flashing yellow light means you must slow down and proceed with caution, watching carefully for cross traffic, pedestrians, or other hazards. You do not have to stop if the way is clear, but you must be prepared to stop if needed.

question: At dusk or on overcast days, what should you do regarding vehicle lighting?
options: a:Turn on your headlights (low beam) so others can see you.,b:Drive using only your parking lights.,c:Not turn on any lights.
note: At dusk, dawn, or on overcast days, you should turn on your low‑beam headlights so other drivers can see you more easily. Parking lights alone are not enough while driving, and driving with no lights in low‑visibility conditions makes it much harder for others to see you and react in time.

question: Which general rule should you follow about passing other vehicles?
options: a:Pass on the right whenever possible.,b:Try to get to the front of slow traffic to see better.,c:Drive with traffic flow and pass only when necessary.
note: Staying with the flow of traffic within the speed limit and passing only when necessary reduces lane changes and speed differences, which lowers collision risk. Passing should be done only when you have a clear need and a safe opportunity, not just to get ahead.

question: What does a regulatory sign with a red circle and a slash through a symbol indicate?
options: a:That some drivers should yield to other drivers.,b:That the action shown is forbidden.,c:That drivers should come to a complete stop.
note: A regulatory sign with a red circle and a diagonal slash over a black symbol means the action shown is prohibited. For example, a right-turn arrow with a red circle and slash means no right turn is allowed at that location.

question: Who should wear seat belts to be most effective?
options: a:All occupants of a vehicle.,b:The driver only.,c:Only passengers on long trips.
note: Seat belts protect all occupants by keeping them in place during a crash, reducing the chance of serious injury or death. Unbelted passengers can be thrown around inside the vehicle and can injure themselves and others, so everyone should be properly buckled.

question: On a two-lane street being followed by a fire engine that is NOT using lights or siren, you should:
options: a:Speed up to get out of its way.,b:Stop as quickly as you can.,c:Continue to drive in a normal manner.
note: Emergency vehicles only require you to yield and pull over when they are using their lights and siren. If a fire engine behind you is not using them, treat it like any other vehicle and continue driving normally while obeying all traffic laws.

question: When is it appropriate to use your horn?
options: a:Only when passing another car.,b:To alert others if you lose control or to avoid a collision.,c:To express frustration at other drivers.
note: Your horn is a safety device used to warn others of possible danger, such as when you might collide or if your vehicle becomes hard to control. It should not be used to show anger or annoyance, as that can startle other drivers and create unsafe situations.

question: When a school bus is stopped with red lights flashing, what must you do?
options: a:Pass if the bus is on the opposite side of a divided highway only.,b:Proceed slowly if you do not see children.,c:Stop — it is illegal to pass the bus.
note: When a school bus has its red lights flashing, you must stop and remain stopped until the lights stop flashing and it is safe to proceed. This applies to traffic in both directions unless you are on the opposite side of a divided highway with a physical barrier or unpaved median; in that case, oncoming traffic is usually not required to stop.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: How would you best define a speed limit?
options: a:The suggested speed only for heavy vehicles.,b:The recommended safe speed under all conditions.,c:The maximum or minimum legal speed you may travel under ideal conditions.
note: A speed limit is the maximum (or sometimes minimum, when posted) legal speed allowed under ideal conditions. You must slow down below the posted limit when conditions such as rain, snow, fog, heavy traffic, or poor visibility make the posted speed unsafe.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: How close to the right edge of the road should your vehicle be when preparing to make a right turn?
options: a:As close as is safely practicable to the right-hand curb or edge of the roadway.,b:Remain in the center of your lane regardless of the turn.,c:Stay at least several feet away from the right edge to leave room for other vehicles to pass on the right.
note: For a right turn, you should move as close as is safely practicable to the right-hand curb or edge of the roadway, not a fixed distance like one, three, or five feet. Hugging the right edge reduces the chance another vehicle, bicycle, or motorcycle will try to pass you on the right and helps you turn into the correct lane.

question: Which statement best describes a drowsy driver?
options: a:Opening a window and turning up the radio will keep them alert.,b:Drinking strong coffee is an effective long-term solution.,c:Drowsy drivers can perform so poorly that their driving may resemble that of a drunk driver.
note: Drowsy drivers can be as dangerous as drunk drivers. Fatigue slows reaction time, narrows attention, and can cause “microsleeps” where you briefly fall asleep at the wheel. Tricks like opening a window, turning up the radio, or drinking coffee may help only briefly; the only real solution is rest and not driving when you are too tired.

question: If convicted of passing a stopped school bus with its red warning lights activated, you will:
options: a:Receive only a written warning.,b:Be required to pay a substantial fine and have five points added to your driving record.,c:Receive two points on your license.
note: Passing a stopped school bus with its red warning lights activated is a serious violation. In Vermont, this offense carries a substantial fine and five points on your driving record, reflecting the high risk it poses to children boarding or leaving the bus.

question: What can happen if you drink alcohol while taking prescription or over-the-counter medicine?
options: a:The medicine will cancel the alcohol's effects.,b:The combination can multiply the impairing effects of both the alcohol and the medicine.,c:Alcohol helps the medicine work faster.
note: Alcohol can interact with both prescription and over‑the‑counter medicines in a way that increases drowsiness, slows reaction time, and impairs judgment more than either substance alone. This combination can also cause dangerous side effects such as dizziness, fainting, or breathing problems, so you should avoid driving if you have mixed alcohol with any medication that can affect alertness.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: What do speed limit signs indicate?
options: a:The maximum or minimum speed that is legally allowed to be driven.,b:Potential driving speeds for the area,c:The speed drivers should drive in heavy traffic.
note: A speed limit sign shows the maximum legal speed under ideal conditions, and in some areas it may also show a minimum speed. You must slow down below the posted limit whenever conditions such as rain, fog, traffic, or road work make the posted speed unsafe, even though it is still the legal maximum.

question: After a stopped school bus has finished unloading children, what should you do?
options: a:Proceed only after the bus driver waves at you.,b:Accelerate quickly to clear the bus area.,c:Watch for children walking along the roadside and proceed cautiously.
note: After the school bus turns off its red lights and you are legally allowed to proceed, you must still move slowly and be prepared to stop. Children may cross the street unexpectedly or walk along the edge of the road, so scan carefully around the bus and proceed with extra caution.

question: Which recommendation does NOT help safe night driving?
options: a:Being aware that dark-tinted windows reduce nighttime visibility.,b:Carrying a flashlight in your vehicle.,c:Keeping your windshield dirty so glare is reduced.
note: For safe night driving, keep your windshield clean inside and out, because dirt and film increase glare from headlights and streetlights and reduce how well you can see. Dark window tint can further reduce visibility at night, so be aware of its effect. Carrying a flashlight can be helpful if you must stop or walk outside your vehicle in the dark, but you should never keep your windshield dirty to reduce glare.

question: On a road without sidewalks, which way should a pedestrian walk?
options: a:Facing oncoming traffic (on the left side of the road).,b:With the flow of traffic (on the right side).,c:On the side with the lightest traffic.
note: On roads without sidewalks, pedestrians should walk on the left side of the road facing oncoming traffic. This lets them see approaching vehicles and move out of the way if needed, which is safer than walking with traffic coming from behind.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When merging onto a freeway, what is usually the best approach?
options: a:Proceed slowly while waiting for a large gap.,b:Turn on your hazard lights while merging.,c:Use the on-ramp to accelerate to the speed of freeway traffic and merge when safe.
note: When entering a freeway, use the on‑ramp/acceleration lane to reach the speed of traffic already on the freeway, check mirrors and blind spots, signal, and merge only when there is a safe gap. Vehicles entering the freeway must yield to traffic already on it.

question: What do double solid yellow lines down the middle of the road mean?
options: a:Indication of a railroad crossing ahead.,b:Passing is not allowed from either direction.,c:Only pedestrians may cross here.
note: Double solid yellow lines separate traffic moving in opposite directions and mean you must not pass from either direction. You may cross them only to make a left turn or to enter/exit a driveway or side road when it is safe and legal, but not to overtake and pass another vehicle.

question: An octagonal traffic sign always means:
options: a:A hospital sign.,b:A stop sign.,c:A speed limit sign.
note: An eight‑sided (octagonal) sign is reserved exclusively for STOP signs. When you see this shape, you must come to a complete stop at the limit line, crosswalk, or before entering the intersection, and proceed only when it is safe.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When entering a busy freeway, what should you do to merge safely?
options: a:Use the acceleration lane to adjust your speed to match freeway traffic.,b:Yield to freeway traffic without attempting to match speed.,c:Enter the freeway slowly and then accelerate after merging.
note: On a busy freeway, use the acceleration lane to reach a speed that matches the flow of traffic, signal, check mirrors and blind spots, and then merge into a safe gap. Always yield to vehicles already on the freeway.

question: How must you respond when you approach a railroad crossing with flashing warning signals?
options: a:Stop and look for a train, obeying the crossing warnings.,b:Slow down and look for a train but continue if the way looks clear.,c:Look for a train, then speed up to cross quickly.
note: Flashing lights or lowered gates at a railroad crossing mean a train is approaching. You must stop, typically no closer than 15 feet from the nearest rail, and remain stopped until the lights stop flashing, the gates are fully raised, and you are sure no other train is coming.

question: When you pass a horse and rider on the road, what should you do?
options: a:Pass quickly to reduce time near the horse.,b:Sound your horn to warn the rider of your approach.,c:Slow down
note: Horses can be easily startled by noise and fast‑moving vehicles. When you see a horse and rider, slow down well in advance, give them plenty of space, and pass very cautiously. Avoid using your horn or accelerating suddenly, because that can frighten the horse and create a dangerous situation for the rider and nearby traffic.

question: How should you adjust your following distance when driving on slippery roads?
options: a:Reduce your following distance to improve traffic flow.,b:Use cruise control to maintain a steady distance.,c:Increase your following distance and reduce speed.
note: On slippery roads, your tires have less traction, so it takes longer to stop and easier to skid. You should slow down and increase your following distance so you have more time and space to react. Avoid using cruise control on slippery surfaces so you can adjust speed smoothly and maintain better control of the vehicle.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: Is it legal to pass by crossing a double solid yellow centerline?
options: a:If there is no oncoming traffic.,b:No.,c:Yes.
note: A double solid yellow centerline means passing is not allowed for traffic in either direction. You must stay in your lane and may not cross the lines to pass another vehicle. The only common exceptions are when you are turning left into or out of a driveway, side road, or making another legal left turn, and when directed by law enforcement or to avoid an immediate hazard.

question: What is the effect of eating or drinking while driving?
options: a:Make no driving errors.,b:Are better drivers because they are not hungry.,c:Are more likely to make driving errors because of the distraction.
note: Eating or drinking while driving is a form of distracted driving. It takes at least one hand off the wheel and often draws your eyes and attention away from the road. This increases the chance of making mistakes, reacting too slowly, or not seeing hazards in time, so drivers who eat or drink while driving are more likely to make driving errors.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: If stopped by a police officer, what is the recommended behavior?
options: a:Get your paperwork ready before the officer reaches your car.,b:Unbuckle your seat belt and lower your window.,c:Stay in your vehicle with your hands visible on the steering wheel and wait for the officer to approach.
note: If you are stopped by a police officer, you should pull over safely, put the vehicle in park, and stay inside with your seat belt fastened. Keep your hands clearly visible on the steering wheel and wait for the officer to approach and give instructions. Avoid reaching for documents until the officer asks, so your movements are not misunderstood and the stop remains safe for everyone.

question: For a driver age 21 or older, at what minimum BAC is it illegal to operate a motor vehicle?
options: a:0.05 percent.,b:0.08 percent.,c:0.02 percent.
note: For drivers 21 and older in most U.S. states, it is illegal to drive with a blood alcohol concentration (BAC) of 0.08% or higher. Even lower levels can be dangerous, but 0.08% is the standard legal limit for DUI for adults.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When preparing to make a left turn, what should drivers do?
options: a:Watch for oncoming vehicles and pedestrians and yield when necessary.,b:Move into the left lane and signal.,c:Slow down gradually while checking their rearview mirror only.
note: When preparing for a left turn, you must signal, move into the proper lane in advance, and most importantly watch for oncoming traffic, cyclists, and pedestrians. You must yield to oncoming vehicles and pedestrians in the crosswalk before turning when it is safe.

question: Drivers should know that large trucks:
options: a:Have large blind spots and require more room to maneuver and stop.,b:Can stop more quickly than passenger vehicles.,c:Do not need extra room to maneuver compared with passenger cars.
note: Large trucks have big blind spots directly behind, along both sides, and in front of the cab. They also need more distance to turn, change lanes, and come to a stop because of their size and weight. Give trucks extra space and avoid lingering in their blind spots.

question: What should you do after rain begins while driving?
options: a:Drive at the posted maximum speed.,b:Increase your speed to reduce time in the rain.,c:Slow down and turn on your headlights so others can see you.
note: When rain begins, the road can be especially slippery as oil and dirt mix with water. You should slow down and turn on your headlights so you can see and be seen. If visibility becomes very poor, pull over safely and wait for conditions to improve.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: If you are already within an intersection and the light turns yellow, when may you continue through?
options: a:If you are already in the intersection when the light turns yellow and can clear it safely.,b:If you can stop safely before entering the intersection, you should do so instead of continuing.,c:You must not enter the intersection on a yellow light if you can safely stop before the stop line.
note: If you are already in the intersection when the light turns yellow, you should continue through and clear the intersection safely; you should not stop in the middle. The decision is based on your position and safety, not on whether you are turning right, an emergency vehicle is present, or pedestrians are crossing.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: What does a yield sign require you to do?
options: a:Yield to traffic in the roadway you are entering or to traffic already in the intersection.,b:Always stop before entering the intersection.,c:Yield only to traffic on the right.
note: A yield sign means you must slow down, be ready to stop, and give the right‑of‑way to traffic and pedestrians already in the intersection or on the road you are entering. If there is no traffic, you may proceed without stopping, but you must always be prepared to stop.

question: Why should drivers be especially alert for motorcyclists, bicyclists, and pedestrians?
options: a:Because they always have different traffic laws.,b:Because they always have the right-of-way.,c:Because they are smaller and more difficult to see in traffic.
note: Motorcycles, bicycles, and pedestrians are smaller and can be hidden in traffic or blind spots, so they are harder to see and more vulnerable in a crash. Drivers must scan carefully and check mirrors and blind spots to spot them early and give them extra space.

question: When should you use high-beam headlights at night?
options: a:When you are following another vehicle closely.,b:When meeting an oncoming vehicle.,c:When driving in open country where there are few other vehicles.
note: Use high‑beam headlights on open roads at night when there are few or no other vehicles, so you can see farther ahead. Dim your high beams when you are following another vehicle closely or when an oncoming vehicle is within range, to avoid blinding other drivers.

question: If an approaching driver fails to dim high-beam headlights, where should you look?
options: a:Toward the left side of the road.,b:At the wheels of the approaching vehicle.,c:Toward the right side of the road.
note: If an oncoming driver does not dim their high beams, avoid looking directly at the glare. Instead, glance toward the right edge of your lane or the right side of the road and use it as a guide while you continue driving safely.

question: When you hear the siren of a fire engine behind you, what must you do?
options: a:Drive with your flashers on.,b:Pull over to the side of the road and stop.,c:Slow down until it passes you.
note: When an emergency vehicle approaches with its siren and lights on, you must yield the right‑of‑way by pulling as far to the right side of the road as safely possible and stopping until it has passed. This creates a clear path so the emergency vehicle can move quickly and safely.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: What is the correct sequence of actions when changing lanes?
options: a:Check mirrors,b:Signal,c:Signal, check mirrors, check blind spot, then change lanes.
note: The correct sequence for changing lanes is: first turn on your signal to communicate your intention, then check your rearview and side mirrors, and finally look over your shoulder to check your blind spot before moving. Signaling comes before checking and moving so other drivers have time to react to your lane change.

question: What is the effect of combining alcohol with drugs?
options: a:It decreases the effects of both.,b:It helps cure your illness.,c:It can increase the effects of both the alcohol and the drugs.
note: Combining alcohol with many legal or illegal drugs can greatly increase the effects of both substances. This can slow your reaction time, impair judgment, and make you much less able to control your vehicle safely. Because of this, you should never drive after mixing alcohol with any drug that can affect the brain or body.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: From a center left-turn lane, which maneuvers are permitted?
options: a:Using the lane to pass slow-moving traffic.,b:Driving straight through the intersection.,c:Making left turns from either direction; you may enter the lane briefly to prepare for or complete a left turn.
note: A center left‑turn lane is only for making left turns from either direction or for beginning a left turn out of a driveway or side street. You may not use it to pass other vehicles or to continue straight through an intersection. Enter the lane shortly before your turn, signal, and complete your left turn safely.

question: You arrive at an intersection with a flashing red light. What must you do?
options: a:Slow down and yield to traffic then go.,b:Wait for a flashing green light.,c:Come to a complete stop and proceed when safe.
note: A flashing red light is treated like a stop sign. You must come to a complete stop at the limit line, crosswalk, or before entering the intersection. After stopping, look for other vehicles, pedestrians, and bicycles, and proceed only when the intersection is clear and it is safe to go.

question: How can you reduce your risk of hydroplaning?
options: a:Drive more slowly in wet conditions.,b:Drive faster to get through water quickly.,c:Drive through deep water to clear tires.
note: Hydroplaning happens when your tires ride on top of water and lose contact with the road, causing a loss of steering and braking control. To reduce this risk, slow down in wet conditions, especially in heavy rain or standing water, and make sure your tires are properly inflated and have good tread.

question: Which substances may impair your ability to drive and lead to DUII?
options: a:Alcohol, illegal drugs, inhalants, and certain prescription or over-the-counter medicines.,b:Only beer and wine.,c:Only illicit hard drugs.
note: Alcohol, illegal drugs, inhalants, and many prescription or over‑the‑counter medicines can all slow your reactions, affect judgment, and reduce coordination. Any substance that impairs your ability to drive safely can lead to a DUI/DUII charge, even if it was legally obtained.

question: Which of these actions reduces your risk of hydroplaning on wet roads?
options: a:Only replace tires with bad tread.,b:Slow down on wet roads, maintain proper tire pressure, and replace tires with worn tread.,c:Only maintain correct tire pressure.
note: Hydroplaning happens when your tires ride on a thin layer of water and lose contact with the road. You reduce this risk by slowing down on wet roads, keeping your tires properly inflated, and replacing tires with worn tread so they can channel water away.

question: In what ways can alcoholic beverages affect your driving?
options: a:It gives you a feeling of false confidence.,b:It impairs your thinking ability.,c:It slows your reaction time.,d:All of the above.
note: Alcohol affects driving in several ways at the same time: it can give you a false sense of confidence so you take more risks, it impairs your thinking and judgment so you make poor decisions, and it slows your reaction time so you cannot respond quickly to hazards. Because all of these effects are dangerous, any amount of drinking can reduce driving safety.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: If entering the roadway from a driveway or private road, what should you do?
options: a:Force your way into traffic if necessary.,b:Assume you have the right-of-way.,c:Yield to drivers already on the public road.
note: When you enter a public road from a driveway, alley, or private road, you must yield to all traffic already on the roadway, including vehicles, bicycles, and pedestrians. Wait until it is safe, then enter without forcing other road users to slow or change lanes suddenly.

question: What factors determine how much space you need to cross traffic safely?
options: a:The use of your turn signal.,b:Whether a stop sign is present.,c:Road and weather conditions, and the speed and distance of oncoming vehicles.
note: To cross traffic safely, you must have enough time and space based on several factors: road and weather conditions (which affect traction and acceleration), how far away other vehicles are, and how fast they are approaching. Poor conditions or faster traffic mean you need a larger gap before crossing.

question: At night, which road users are hardest to see?
options: a:Pedestrians.,b:Road signs.,c:Other motorists.
note: Pedestrians are much harder to see at night than reflective road signs or vehicles with lights. They may wear dark clothing and are not illuminated, so you must use low- and high-beam headlights correctly, reduce speed, and scan carefully for people near the roadway.

question: How should you prepare when driving to an unfamiliar area?
options: a:Plan your trip in advance and check maps or directions before you go.,b:Depend solely on road signs as you drive.,c:Drive without a clear idea of your destination.
note: Planning your trip in advance and checking maps or directions helps you avoid last‑second lane changes, sudden stops, and distractions from trying to navigate while driving. Knowing your route before you start allows you to focus on traffic and drive more safely in unfamiliar areas.

question: What is the primary cause of hydroplaning?
options: a:Only worn brakes.,b:Driving too fast on a wet surface so the tires cannot clear water effectively.,c:Sudden stops alone.
note: Hydroplaning happens when you drive too fast on a wet surface and your tires cannot push water out of the way. A thin layer of water builds under the tires, lifting them off the road so you lose traction and steering control. Slowing down in rain and keeping tires in good condition greatly reduces this risk.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: If you pass your exit while on the interstate, what should you do?
options: a:Quickly cut across traffic to make your turn.,b:Make a U-turn to go back to the exit.,c:Continue driving and use the next exit.
note: If you miss your exit on an interstate, you must continue to the next exit. Never stop, back up, cut across the median, or make a U‑turn on the highway, as these actions are illegal and extremely dangerous. Exit safely at the next opportunity and then find a route back to your intended exit.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: What must you do when turning or changing lanes?
options: a:Only signal if other vehicles are visible.,b:Only signal at night.,c:Always signal your intention
note: You must always signal before turning or changing lanes, even if you think no one else is around. Turn signals communicate your intentions to other drivers, cyclists, and pedestrians, giving them time to react and helping prevent collisions.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When you see a merging traffic sign on a multilane roadway, what should you do?
options: a:Move over one lane when safe to make room for entering vehicles.,b:Honk at incoming traffic to warn them.,c:Always remain at your present speed.
note: A merging traffic sign warns that vehicles will be entering your lane from an on‑ramp. On a multilane road, you should help create a smooth, safe merge by moving over one lane when it is safe, or by adjusting your speed to allow space. Never rely on holding your speed and forcing merging drivers to fit in.

question: Why must other drivers allow extra room around heavy trucks?
options: a:The decreased stopping distance required by large vehicles.,b:The increased stopping distance required by large vehicles.,c:The decreased noise of larger vehicles.
note: Large trucks are heavier and need a much longer distance to stop than passenger cars. Other drivers should leave extra space in front of and around trucks so the truck driver has enough room to brake and maneuver safely.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When may you make a right turn at a solid red light?
options: a:After coming to a complete stop, yielding to pedestrians and vehicles, unless a sign prohibits the turn.,b:Any time traffic is light.,c:Only when a police officer signals you to turn.
note: Unless posted otherwise, you may turn right on red after a full stop and after yielding to pedestrians and other traffic.

question: What will help someone overcome the effects of alcoholic drinks?
options: a:Drinking tomato juice and lime.,b:Drinking hot coffee or getting fresh air.,c:Only the passage of time.
note: Once alcohol is in the bloodstream, only time allows your body to process and eliminate it. Coffee, cold showers, food, or fresh air may make someone feel more awake, but they do not reduce blood alcohol concentration or restore driving ability.

question: If an aggressive driver cuts you off, what is the advisable response?
options: a:Flash lights and yell to teach them a lesson.,b:Immediately call the aggressive driver names while driving.,c:Stay calm and move out of the aggressive driver's way.
