note: If another driver behaves aggressively or cuts you off, the safest response is to stay calm, avoid eye contact or gestures, and create space by safely slowing down or changing lanes. Do not retaliate, as that can escalate the situation and increase the risk of a crash.

question: If you leave your vehicle unattended, what actions are required?
options: a:Turn off the engine only.,b:Lock the ignition and remove the key, stop the engine, and set the parking brake.,c:Set the parking brake only.
note: When leaving your vehicle, stop the engine, lock the ignition, remove the key, and set the parking brake to secure the vehicle.

question: How should you behave when you see a school crossing sign?
options: a:Watch carefully for children and be prepared to stop.,b:Always come to a stop whether a sign or not.,c:Always sound your horn to warn children.
note: A school crossing sign warns that children may be crossing the road. You should slow down, watch carefully for children, and be prepared to stop if they are in or near the crosswalk. You are not required to stop if no children are present, and you should not use your horn unless needed to avoid a collision.

question: What does a single broken white line between lanes mean?
options: a:Lanes are moving in the same direction and passing is prohibited.,b:Lanes are moving in opposite directions and you may pass when safe.,c:Lanes are moving in the same direction and you may pass when it is safe to do so.
note: A single broken white line separates lanes of traffic moving in the same direction. You may change lanes or pass across this line when it is safe and legal to do so. It does not separate opposite directions of travel, and it does not prohibit passing.

question: How should you check blind spots before changing lanes?
options: a:Use only the outside mirror on the side you intend to move toward.,b:Rely only on the inside rearview mirror.,c:Turn your head and look over your shoulder to verify the blind spot.
note: Mirrors do not show areas directly alongside and slightly behind your vehicle, known as blind spots. Before changing lanes, you must briefly turn your head and look over your shoulder in the direction you want to move to make sure no vehicle, motorcycle, bicycle, or person is in your blind spot.

question: When driving in regular traffic, what speed strategy is generally safest?
options: a:Drive faster than the surrounding traffic to get through quickly.,b:Drive significantly slower than other vehicles to be cautious.,c:Drive with the flow of traffic while staying within the posted speed limit.
note: The safest strategy in normal traffic is to move with the general flow while staying at or below the posted speed limit. Driving much faster increases crash risk and tickets, and driving much slower than surrounding traffic can cause sudden braking, lane changes, and rear-end collisions.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When entering heavy interstate traffic from an entrance ramp, who has the right-of-way?
options: a:Drivers already on the interstate.,b:The entering driver has the right-of-way.,c:Interstate drivers must wave entering drivers into traffic.
note: On entrance ramps, the vehicles already on the interstate have the right-of-way. The entering driver must adjust speed, signal, and merge only when there is a safe gap, yielding to traffic already on the highway.

question: If it starts to sleet or snow while driving, what should you do?
options: a:Speed up to get out of the area quickly.,b:Ignore other vehicles nearby.,c:Keep windshield and mirrors clear and increase following distance.
note: In sleet or snow, traction and visibility are reduced. You should keep your windshield and mirrors clear, slow down, and increase your following distance so you have more time and space to stop on slippery roads.

question: Which traffic signal requires you to come to a complete stop, yield to cross traffic and pedestrians, and then proceed when clear?
options: a:Solid green light.,b:Flashing yellow light.,c:Flashing red light.
note: A flashing red light is treated the same as a stop sign. You must come to a complete stop, check for cross traffic and pedestrians, yield as needed, and then proceed only when the way is clear.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When must you pull over and allow an emergency vehicle with lights and siren to pass?
options: a:Only if it is following you.,b:Only if it is approaching from the opposite direction.,c:In most situations, regardless of the emergency vehicle's direction of travel; on divided highways with a median, oncoming traffic usually is not required to stop.
note: When an emergency vehicle approaches with lights and siren, you must yield the right-of-way by pulling as far to the right as possible and stopping until it has passed. This generally applies regardless of the vehicle’s direction of travel, but on divided highways with a median or barrier, oncoming traffic in the opposite lanes is usually not required to stop unless directed by an officer.

question: When must you stop for a school bus?
options: a:If you are driving on a two-lane highway and its red lights are flashing.,b:That is parked on the shoulder of the road with no one in it.,c:Whenever a school bus is moving toward you, even if its red lights are not flashing.
note: You must stop for a school bus that is stopped with flashing red lights (and often a stop arm extended) when you are on a two-lane road or an undivided roadway; traffic in both directions must stop. You do not have to stop for a bus that is merely approaching you but still moving without its red lights activated.

question: Why must you be cautious when passing a bicyclist?
options: a:Because bicycles are always traveling faster than cars.,b:Oncoming traffic may not see you pull out to pass, and bicyclists may suddenly swerve to avoid hazards.,c:Bicyclists always have the right-of-way and you must stop.
note: When passing a bicyclist, you must be cautious because they can suddenly swerve to avoid potholes, debris, or opening car doors, and you also need enough room so oncoming traffic can clearly see you and you can return to your lane safely. Always give cyclists plenty of space and only pass when it is safe for both you and oncoming traffic.

question: What do pennant-shaped traffic signs indicate?
options: a:School zones.,b:No passing zones.,c:Speed limits.
note: Pennant-shaped signs are posted on the left side of the road and mark the beginning of a no passing zone. They warn you not to start or continue a pass in that area because it is unsafe to do so.

question: What is a 'No zone' with respect to large vehicles?
options: a:A one-way traffic area.,b:The blind spot area around a truck or large vehicle.,c:A designated no-passing zone.
note: A 'No Zone' is the large blind spot around trucks and other big vehicles where the driver cannot see you in their mirrors. Staying out of these areas—especially directly behind, alongside the trailer, and close in front—helps ensure the truck driver can see you and reduces the risk of a collision.

question: Where is it best to keep a space cushion around your vehicle?
options: a:Only on the left and right sides of your vehicle.,b:Only behind your vehicle.,c:On all sides of your vehicle.
note: A space cushion is the open space around your vehicle that gives you time to react. Keeping space in front, behind, and on both sides lets you brake, change lanes, or steer around hazards more safely and reduces the chance of a collision.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When parking downhill on a two-way street, which way should you turn your wheels?
options: a:Turn your wheels to the left.,b:Turn your wheels to the right so the vehicle will roll away from traffic if it moves.,c:Keep your wheels straight ahead.
note: When parking facing downhill on a two-way street with a curb, turn your front wheels toward the curb (to the right). If the vehicle rolls, it will move into the curb instead of into traffic, reducing the risk of it rolling into the roadway.

question: When must a driver change lanes to create space for a stopped emergency or maintenance vehicle?
options: a:When approaching a stopped vehicle using flashing blue,b:When approaching a stopped maintenance vehicle using flashing amber lights.,c:When approaching a stopped police vehicle using flashing blue lights.
note: You must move over a lane to provide space for stopped police (blue), emergency (red), or maintenance/roadside assistance (amber) vehicles when safe to do so.

question: If an oncoming vehicle is heading into your lane, what is the recommended immediate action?
options: a:Blow your horn,b:Steer right and brake firmly while using your horn.,c:Brake lightly and hold your lane.
note: If an oncoming vehicle is drifting or heading into your lane, immediately use your horn to get the driver’s attention, then steer to the right side of your lane or onto the right shoulder if needed, and brake firmly. Do not swerve left into the oncoming lane, because that can put you directly in the path of other vehicles and make a collision more likely.

question: If you borrow an unfamiliar vehicle, what should you do before driving it?
options: a:Assume all vehicles are identical and start driving.,b:Take a few minutes to locate and learn how to operate the controls and correct any obvious defects before driving.,c:Disregard any defects to avoid embarrassing the owner.
note: Before driving an unfamiliar vehicle, take a few minutes to adjust the seat and mirrors and locate and learn how to operate the lights, wipers, turn signals, gear selector, parking brake, and horn. If you notice any obvious safety defects, such as bad tires or inoperative lights, they should be corrected before you drive.

question: What is the most common cause of traffic crashes?
options: a:Human error.,b:Bad weather.,c:New drivers.
note: Most crashes are caused by human error, such as inattention, distraction, following too closely, misjudging gaps or speed, or failing to yield. While weather and inexperience can contribute, driver decisions and mistakes are the primary cause of traffic collisions.

question: Lanes of traffic moving in opposite directions are divided by what color lines?
options: a:White lines.,b:Red lines.,c:Yellow lines.
note: Yellow pavement lines separate traffic moving in opposite directions. White lines separate lanes of traffic moving in the same direction, and are also used for edge lines on the right side of the roadway.

question: When confronted with an oncoming car on your left and a bicyclist on your right, how should you proceed?
options: a:Split the difference and squeeze between them.,b:Pull onto the shoulder.,c:Let the oncoming car pass first, then pass the bicyclist when it is safe.
note: When you face hazards on both sides, you should not try to squeeze between them. Focus on one hazard at a time: slow down, let the oncoming car pass first, then move over and pass the bicyclist only when you can give them plenty of space. This reduces the chance of a collision with either the car or the cyclist.

question: How can you ensure your physical condition won’t impair your driving?
options: a:Ignore minor health warnings when driving.,b:Only drive when you feel strong.,c:Know how any medicine affects your driving and drive within your limitations.
note: Your physical and medical condition directly affect your driving. You should understand how any medications (including over‑the‑counter drugs) affect alertness, vision, and coordination, and only drive when you are fit to do so. Regular checkups and honest self‑assessment help you stay within your physical limitations and avoid driving when it is unsafe.

question: Which of the following about winter driving is NOT true?
options: a:Winter is the most difficult driving season.,b:Check antifreeze and washer fluid levels before winter driving.,c:Using cruise control in winter weather is safe.
note: In winter, roads can be icy, snowy, or wet, making traction and visibility worse. You should check antifreeze and washer fluid before winter driving and use extra caution. Cruise control should not be used on slippery surfaces because it can cause you to lose control if the wheels start to slip.

question: Which is the safest way to drive through a curve?
options: a:Maintain a constant speed throughout no matter the conditions.,b:Speed up as you enter and slow down as you exit.,c:Slow down as you enter the curve and gradually speed up as you exit.
note: Before entering a curve, slow down so you can steer smoothly and keep traction. Once you are past the sharpest part of the curve and can see the road ahead, gently accelerate as you exit. Entering too fast or accelerating into the curve makes it easier to skid or run off the road.

question: When does your vehicle's stopping distance increase?
options: a:On paved highways in good weather.,b:Only when driving at night.,c:On wet or icy roads.
note: Stopping distance is longer whenever traction or visibility is reduced. Wet, icy, or otherwise slippery roads greatly increase the distance it takes to stop because your tires cannot grip the road as well. You should slow down and increase your following distance in these conditions.

question: Lack of sleep affects driving ability similarly to what?
options: a:The effects of being angry.,b:The effects of amphetamines.,c:The effects of alcohol.
note: Lack of sleep slows reaction time, reduces awareness, and impairs judgment in ways very similar to alcohol. After many hours awake, your driving performance can resemble that of a driver over the legal blood alcohol limit, so fatigue must be treated as seriously as drunk driving.

question: Which practice helps prevent drowsiness on long trips?
options: a:Reducing your speed significantly.,b:Keeping the radio on loud.,c:Stopping regularly to rest and stretch.
note: On long trips, the safest way to fight drowsiness is to stop regularly to rest, walk, and stretch. Loud music or just slowing down does not keep you alert and can give a false sense of safety. Plan breaks before you feel very tired, and switch drivers if possible.

question: If your wheels drop off the pavement onto the shoulder, what should you do?
options: a:Stop your car on the edge of the road.,b:Slow down and very carefully steer back onto the pavement.,c:Brake hard and turn sharply back onto the pavement.
note: If your wheels drop off the pavement, stay calm, ease off the gas, and slow down gradually without jerking the wheel or slamming the brakes. When the car is under control and your speed is reduced, gently steer back onto the pavement when it is safe and traffic allows.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When making a turn, how should you adjust your speed?
options: a:Maintain your speed.,b:Vary your speed so you reduce it to a safe turning pace.,c:Increase your speed.
note: Before entering a turn, slow down to a speed that lets you stay in your lane and react to hazards. Enter the turn at this safe speed, then gently accelerate as you exit if conditions allow. Turning too fast can cause skidding or loss of control.

question: Which statement about work zones is correct?
options: a:They are marked with black and white signs only.,b:Drivers are not required to slow down in work zones.,c:Work zones may be stationary or moving and are marked with orange signs.
note: Work zones can be either stationary (like a fixed construction site) or moving (such as a line-painting truck) and are identified by orange signs and devices. In these areas you must slow down, obey posted work zone speed limits, and be prepared for workers, equipment, and sudden lane changes.

question: Two solid yellow lines on the pavement indicate what?
options: a:Passing is allowed from both directions.,b:You may pass when at the top of a hill.,c:Passing is not permitted.
note: Two solid yellow center lines mean vehicles traveling in either direction may not cross the lines to pass. You must stay in your lane and only cross these lines when making a permitted left turn or when directed by traffic control.

question: When changing lanes, what are important actions to take?
options: a:Make sure the lane is clear before entering.,b:Check your blind spot.,c:Signal your intentions ahead of the lane change.
note: A safe lane change requires all three actions together: signal well in advance to communicate your intentions, check your mirrors, and quickly look over your shoulder to check your blind spot. Only after you are sure the lane is clear should you move into it smoothly.

question: What lighting should you use when driving in rainy conditions?
options: a:Low beam headlights.,b:High beams.,c:Parking lights only.
note: In rain, always use low beam headlights. Low beams help you see the road and make your vehicle more visible to others without causing glare. High beams can reflect off rain, fog, or mist and actually reduce your ability to see.

question: Which statement about driving on wet roads is correct?
options: a:Deep water is less hazardous than shallow water.,b:Water does not affect vehicles with good tires.,c:As your speed increases, your tires are more likely to lose contact with the road and hydroplane.
note: As your speed increases on a wet road, your tires have less time to channel water away, which increases the risk of hydroplaning. Hydroplaning happens when your tires ride on top of a thin layer of water instead of gripping the road, causing a loss of steering and braking control. Slowing down in wet conditions greatly reduces this risk.

question: What is the only effective way to reduce your blood alcohol concentration (BAC)?
options: a:Exercise.,b:Allow your body time to get rid of the alcohol.,c:Drink coffee.
note: The only way to lower your blood alcohol concentration is to allow enough time for your body to process and eliminate the alcohol. Coffee, exercise, cold showers, or other tricks may make you feel more awake, but they do not speed up how quickly your liver metabolizes alcohol or make you safer to drive.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When a traffic light turns from green to yellow as you approach an intersection, what should you do?
options: a:Speed up to beat the red light.,b:Apply the brakes sharply to stop immediately.,c:Be prepared to stop safely.
note: A steady yellow light warns that the signal is about to turn red. You should slow down and be prepared to stop if you can do so safely before entering the intersection. Do not speed up to beat the red, and avoid braking so hard that you could lose control or be rear‑ended.

question: What is the best way to handle a driver tailgating you?
options: a:Speed up to widen the gap ahead of you.,b:Slam on your brakes to warn them.,c:Gradually slow down or change lanes to encourage them to pass.
note: If someone is following too closely, keep a steady speed, increase your following distance ahead, and when it is safe, gradually slow or change lanes to let them pass. Do not speed up or brake suddenly, as both can increase the risk of a collision.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When approaching an uncontrolled intersection, you should:
options: a:Yield to all other drivers regardless of position.,b:Yield to vehicles coming from the right and be prepared to stop.,c:Maintain your speed and proceed without checking
note: At an uncontrolled intersection (no signs or signals), you must slow down, look carefully in all directions, and be prepared to stop. Yield the right‑of‑way to vehicles already in the intersection and to vehicles approaching from your right if you arrive at the same time.

question: Traffic signs, signals, and pavement markings must be:
options: a:Merely suggestions to drivers.,b:Always obeyed.,c:Followed only when there is other traffic.
note: Traffic signs, signals, and pavement markings are legal controls that all drivers must obey at all times, whether or not other traffic is present. Ignoring them is both unsafe and against the law.

question: When near a motorcycle, what must you allow the motorcyclist?
options: a:Drive on the shoulder beside the motorcycle.,b:Allow the motorcycle to use a complete lane.,c:Allow the motorcycle to use only half of a lane.
note: Motorcycles are entitled to a full lane of traffic, just like any other motor vehicle. You must allow a motorcycle to use an entire lane and should not crowd or share the lane beside a motorcycle.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: To pass a slower vehicle on a two-lane, two-way road you must:
options: a:Only attempt the pass when it is legal and safe and you can use the oncoming lane to complete the pass.,b:Never cross the centerline to pass.,c:Use the shoulder to pass when it is clear.
note: On a two-lane, two-way road, you may pass a slower vehicle only when it is legal and safe, and only by briefly using the oncoming lane. You must have enough clear distance ahead, obey all pavement markings and signs, and never use the shoulder to pass.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: If a driver's left arm is extended upward, what does that signal mean?
options: a:The driver intends to turn left.,b:The driver plans to stop.,c:The driver intends to turn right.
note: Standard hand signals use the left arm: straight out for a left turn, bent upward at the elbow for a right turn, and bent downward for slowing or stopping. A left arm extended upward means the driver intends to turn right.

question: What does a flashing yellow traffic light require you to do?
options: a:Stop and wait for a green light.,b:Proceed with caution.,c:Yield only to oncoming traffic.
note: A flashing yellow light means you must slow down and proceed with caution, watching carefully for other vehicles and pedestrians. You do not have to stop unless needed for safety or other traffic.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: If a crossing guard is directing traffic in a school zone, what must you do?
options: a:Copy what surrounding traffic is doing,b:Follow the directions given by the crossing guard.,c:Assume the guard is not supposed to be directing traffic.
note: In a school zone, you must always obey the directions of an authorized crossing guard. Their instructions override normal traffic signals and signs, and you must slow down, be prepared to stop, and follow their hand signals to protect children and pedestrians.

question: What is the safest way to pass a bicyclist?
options: a:Honk at the bicyclist to alert them before passing quickly.,b:Slow down and give the bicyclist as much space as possible.,c:Drive in the bicycle lane until you can pass
note: When passing a bicyclist, slow down and leave as much space as possible—many states require at least 3 feet or more. Do not honk in a way that could startle the rider, and never drive in the bicycle lane to pass.

question: If a green arrow for your turn changes to a solid green light, what must you do?
options: a:You still have the right‑of‑way to turn without yielding.,b:You may no longer turn and must proceed straight.,c:You may still turn, but you must first yield to oncoming traffic and pedestrians.
note: When a green arrow changes to a solid green light, you may still turn in the direction of the arrow, but you no longer have a protected turn. You must yield to oncoming traffic, bicyclists, and pedestrians in the crosswalk and only turn when it is safe.

question: A steady yellow traffic signal warns that what will soon appear?
options: a:A steady red light.,b:A flashing yellow.,c:A steady green.
note: A steady yellow light means the signal is about to turn red. You should slow down and stop if you can do so safely; if you are too close to the intersection to stop safely, proceed with caution before the light turns red.

question: Which safety restraint combination provides the most effective protection in a crash?
options: a:Both a lap/shoulder belt and an airbag.,b:Only an airbag.,c:Only a lap belt.
note: The safest protection in a crash is the combination of a lap and shoulder belt used together with an airbag. Airbags are designed to work with seat belts, not replace them, and a lap belt alone does not protect the upper body as well as a full lap/shoulder belt plus airbag.

question: When you see an emergency vehicle using its lights or siren, you must:
options: a:Slow down and keep moving in your lane.,b:Keep driving in your lane and ignore the vehicle.,c:Pull to the right curb and stop.
note: When an emergency vehicle approaches using its lights or siren, you must yield the right‑of‑way by pulling as close as safely possible to the right edge or curb of the road and stopping until the vehicle has passed, unless directed otherwise by a police officer.

question: What should you check before switching on the ignition?
options: a:That you and all passengers have fastened seat belts.,b:That only child passengers have buckled their belts.,c:That only adult passengers have buckled their belts.
note: Develop the habit of buckling your seat belt and ensuring all passengers are belted before starting the vehicle.

question: If another driver is driving aggressively behind you, how should you react?
options: a:Speed up as he or she is passing you.,b:Try to get out of the aggressive driver’s way.,c:Stare at the driver as he or she is passing you.
note: When another driver is aggressive or tailgating, your goal is to avoid a confrontation and reduce risk. Do not speed up or stare at the driver, as this can escalate road rage. Instead, stay calm, signal early, and safely move to another lane or otherwise allow the aggressive driver to pass. Avoid eye contact and focus on keeping space around your vehicle.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: If two drivers arrive simultaneously to an open intersection, who has the right-of-way?
options: a:The driver on the right has the right-of-way.,b:The driver on the left has the right-of-way.,c:One may continue without stopping.
note: When two vehicles arrive at an uncontrolled intersection at the same time, the driver on the left must yield to the driver on the right. This rule helps prevent confusion and collisions. Always approach open intersections slowly and be prepared to yield if another vehicle is already in or clearly entering the intersection.

question: If the driver behind you wants to pass, what should you do?
options: a:Go the same speed.,b:Slow down to allow room in front of your vehicle for the other driver to complete the pass easily.,c:Speed up.
note: If a driver behind you wants to pass, help them do it safely. Maintain a steady speed or slightly slow down to create more space in front of your vehicle so they can return to the lane without cutting too closely in front of you. Never speed up when someone is passing, as this increases the risk of a side‑by‑side collision and lengthens the time both vehicles are in the oncoming lane.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: If you must stop at an intersection that has no stop line or crosswalk, where should you stop?
options: a:In the intersecting roadway to get a better view.,b:Anywhere you choose as long as you slow down,c:At the point nearest the intersecting roadway where you can see approaching traffic without entering the intersection.
note: When there is no stop line or crosswalk, you must still stop before entering the intersection. Stop at the point nearest the intersecting roadway where you have a clear view of approaching traffic, but without actually entering the cross street. This lets you see other vehicles and pedestrians while keeping your vehicle out of their path.

question: If other drivers are acting angrily, what is the best way to protect yourself?
options: a:Avoid making eye contact and do not react with gestures.,b:Engage with them to calm the situation.,c:Physically and mentally distance yourself from the situation.
note: To protect yourself from angry or aggressive drivers, avoid eye contact, do not respond with gestures or words, and do not engage. Keep your attention on the road and drive calmly and predictably. If needed, safely increase the distance between you and the aggressive driver by changing lanes or exiting the roadway, but your first response should be to avoid reacting and not escalate the situation.

question: When stopped in traffic that is crossing railroad tracks with no signals or gates, what must you ensure?
options: a:You may pass slower vehicles while crossing.,b:You have space to fully clear the tracks without stopping.,c:You have the right-of-way so you do not need to check for trains.
note: Before you drive onto railroad tracks, you must be sure there is enough room on the far side to clear the tracks completely without stopping. Never stop on the tracks, and never pass another vehicle while approaching or crossing railroad tracks.

question: Approaching an emergency vehicle stopped with flashing lights, what must you do?
options: a:Stay in your lane and continue to drive at the same speed.,b:Drive to the right side of the road and stop immediately.,c:Slow down and, if possible, move over a lane away from the emergency vehicle.
note: Move over a lane if safe; if not possible, slow down below the posted limit and give the stopped emergency or service vehicle as much room as you can.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When entering interstate traffic from an entrance or acceleration ramp, what should you do?
options: a:Has the right-of-way.,b:May force their way into traffic.,c:Must yield to drivers already on the interstate and merge only when there is a safe gap.
note: Traffic already on the interstate has the right-of-way. When entering from an entrance or acceleration ramp, use the ramp to reach the speed of traffic, signal, and yield until there is a safe gap, then merge smoothly without forcing your way in.

question: Signs that require you to obey specific instructions are called:
options: a:Regulatory signs.,b:Warning signs.,c:Information signs.
note: Regulatory signs tell you about laws and rules you must obey, such as speed limits, stop and yield signs, and lane-use controls. Ignoring these signs can result in traffic tickets or crashes.

question: If an oncoming vehicle is using high beams and fails to dim them, where should you look to avoid being blinded?
options: a:Toward the center of the road.,b:Toward the right side of the road.,c:Either side of the road.
note: If an oncoming driver does not dim their high beams, avoid looking directly at the glare. Instead, glance toward the right edge of your lane or the right side of the road and use it as a guide while you continue driving safely.

question: What are the risks associated with worn or bald tires?
options: a:Can make turning more difficult.,b:Are likely to hydroplane.,c:Can increase your stopping distance.
note: Worn or bald tires are dangerous because they reduce traction. With little or no tread, your vehicle is more likely to hydroplane on wet roads, it takes longer to stop, and the car may not respond as well when you turn or swerve. All of the listed risks are true, but the most direct and serious risk commonly emphasized is the increased chance of hydroplaning.

question: What is the most common color used for general warning road signs?
options: a:Red.,b:Green.,c:Yellow.
note: Most general warning signs in the U.S. are diamond-shaped and yellow with black symbols or wording. These signs alert you to conditions such as curves, intersections, pedestrian crossings, or other potential hazards ahead so you can adjust your driving in time.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: A red flashing traffic light at an intersection has the same meaning as which traffic control device?
options: a:A yield sign.,b:A stop sign.,c:A slow sign.
note: A flashing red light means you must come to a complete stop, just as you would at a stop sign. After stopping, proceed only when the intersection is clear and it is safe to go.

question: Which driving habit helps conserve gasoline?
options: a:Accelerating rapidly whenever possible.,b:Slowing down gradually and avoiding unnecessary braking.,c:Sitting in the driveway with the engine running.
note: To conserve fuel, look ahead, anticipate traffic, and slow down gradually instead of braking hard at the last moment. Smooth, steady driving with fewer rapid accelerations and sudden stops uses less gasoline and reduces wear on your vehicle.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: If an officer is directing traffic at an intersection where lights are working, whose directions should you follow?
options: a:Follow the directions indicated by the traffic light.,b:Honk at the officer to get their attention.,c:Follow the directions given by the officer.
note: When a police officer or other authorized person is directing traffic, you must follow their hand signals and instructions, even if traffic lights or signs indicate something different. The officer’s directions temporarily override normal traffic controls to keep everyone safe and traffic flowing.

question: If you see an animal on the roadway, how should you respond?
options: a:Maintain your speed and pass as closely as possible.,b:Honk your horn repeatedly to scare the animal.,c:Slow down and pass cautiously
note: Slow down and pass animals cautiously, giving them space and time to move. Sudden moves, loud horn use, or passing too closely can startle the animal and cause it to run unpredictably into your path.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: At an uncontrolled intersection where you and another vehicle arrive at the same time, and that vehicle is on your right, what should you do?
options: a:Slow down and yield to the vehicle on your right.,b:Drive into the intersection and make the other vehicle stop.,c:Speed up and get through the intersection.
note: At an uncontrolled intersection, if you and another vehicle arrive at the same time, you must yield to the vehicle on your right. Slow down, be prepared to stop, and allow the vehicle on your right to go first to avoid a collision.

question: Which practices help drive safely at night?
options: a:Only drive if you are tired,b:Turn off headlights in rural areas to see better.,c:Increase your following distance and ensure headlights are working.
note: Night driving requires extra caution: increase your following distance so you have more time to react, and make sure your headlights and other lights are clean and working properly so you can see and be seen.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: If you want to turn left and oncoming traffic is heavy while the light is green, what should you do?
options: a:Remain in the intersection only if necessary and safe, or use the next intersection if needed.,b:Wait at the crosswalk for traffic to clear before entering the intersection.,c:Enter and wait in the center of the intersection until traffic clears.
note: With a green light and heavy oncoming traffic, you may carefully move into the intersection and wait near the center with your wheels straight. When it is safe and oncoming traffic clears—or the light turns yellow/red and opposing traffic stops—complete your left turn.

question: How should you regard railroad crossings in general?
options: a:Safe to cross since trains are rare.,b:As potentially dangerous and requiring caution.,c:Safe places to park.
note: Always treat railroad crossings as hazardous. Slow down, look and listen for trains, and be prepared to stop. Obey all warning signs, lights, and gates, and never assume the tracks are clear just because you do not see a train immediately.

question: What does a broken yellow line alongside a solid yellow line indicate?
options: a:Passing is permitted from the lane next to the solid line.,b:Passing on the left is permitted from either direction.,c:Passing is permitted from the lane next to the broken line.
note: A broken yellow line next to a solid yellow line separates traffic moving in opposite directions. Vehicles on the side with the broken line may cross it to pass when it is safe. Vehicles on the side with the solid line must not cross it to pass.

question: Signs that are orange in color normally indicate:
options: a:Regulatory rules such as speed limits.,b:School zones only.,c:Work zones and temporary traffic control.
note: Orange signs are used for work zones and temporary traffic control. They warn of construction, maintenance, or utility work and alert drivers to slow down, be prepared for lane shifts, and follow directions from signs and flaggers.

question: Which device is commonly used on highways to direct drivers into the proper lanes for turning?
options: a:White lines on the side of the road only.,b:Flashing red lights on the shoulder.,c:Arrows painted on lanes and overhead lane-control arrows.
note: Lane-use arrows painted on the pavement and overhead lane-control arrows show which lanes allow turns or through movements. Drivers must follow these arrows to be in the correct lane before turning or going straight.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: How should you use a freeway exit ramp properly?
options: a:Keep the same speed while on the ramp.,b:Do not slow down until you have moved onto the exit ramp.,c:Slow down before entering the exit ramp.
note: On a freeway, stay at highway speed until you reach the exit ramp, then move into the deceleration lane and slow down on the ramp to the posted exit speed. Slowing on the main freeway before entering the ramp can surprise drivers behind you and increase the risk of a rear-end collision.

question: Where is parking prohibited?
options: a:On a hill under any circumstances.,b:Anywhere inside a parking lot.,c:On a crosswalk or in a marked bicycle lane.
note: Parking is prohibited on crosswalks and in marked bicycle lanes because it blocks pedestrians and cyclists and creates safety hazards. When parking along a curb, you must park close and parallel to the curb as local law specifies, often within about 12 inches.

question: If a tire blows out while you are driving, what should you do?
options: a:Keep driving normally until you reach your destination.,b:Slam on your brakes immediately.,c:Hold the steering wheel firmly and gradually slow to a stop off the road.
note: If a tire blows out, the car may pull to one side. Hold the steering wheel firmly, stay calm, and do not slam on the brakes. Ease your foot off the accelerator, let the vehicle slow down gradually, signal, and steer smoothly to the shoulder or a safe area off the road. Brake gently only after you have the vehicle under control and are moving more slowly.

question: If you start to feel tired while driving, what is the best action?
options: a:Open a window to stay awake.,b:Drink coffee and keep going.,c:Stop driving and rest.
note: When you feel tired while driving, your reaction time and judgment are reduced, and you may even fall asleep briefly without realizing it. Opening a window or drinking coffee cannot fully overcome fatigue. The safest action is to get off the road as soon as you can do so safely, stop driving, and rest or change drivers before continuing.

question: What does a diamond-shaped traffic sign indicate?
options: a:Warning of existing or possible hazards ahead.,b:School zones only.,c:Public recreation areas.
note: Diamond-shaped signs are used for warnings. They alert you to existing or possible hazards or changes in road conditions ahead, such as curves, intersections, pedestrian crossings, or work zones. Seeing a diamond-shaped sign means you should be prepared to slow down, adjust your position, or take other precautions.

question: What single action most reduces your risk of injury or death in a crash?
options: a:Limit your driving to weekdays.,b:Wear your seat belt.,c:Stay in the right lane on multilane highways.
note: Wearing a properly adjusted seat belt greatly reduces the chance of serious injury or death in a crash by keeping you from being thrown around inside the vehicle or ejected. Seat belts work together with airbags and other safety features, and using them every time you drive is one of the most important safety habits you can have.

question: When riding in a vehicle, how should small children be protected?
options: a:They may be safely held by a strong adult.,b:They must be properly restrained in appropriate child seats or safety belts.,c:They can stand on the floor in the back seat if supervised.
note: Small children must always be secured in an appropriate child safety seat or booster seat for their age, height, and weight, and older children must use seat belts. In a crash, an adult cannot safely hold a child, and allowing a child to stand or move around in the vehicle is extremely dangerous. Proper restraints keep children in place and spread crash forces over the strongest parts of their bodies.

question: What does a single broken yellow center line mean?
options: a:Lanes are moving in opposite directions and passing is permitted when safe.,b:Lanes are moving in the same direction and passing is allowed.,c:Lanes are moving in opposite directions and passing is prohibited.
note: A single broken yellow center line separates traffic moving in opposite directions. You may cross this line to pass another vehicle, but only when it is safe and when there is no oncoming traffic or other restriction (such as a no‑passing zone sign).

question: Which behavior is a telltale sign of a drunk driver?
options: a:Driving more slowly than traffic at all times.,b:Weaving between lanes.,c:Signaling correctly when changing lanes.
note: Weaving between lanes is a classic sign of impaired driving because the driver has poor control and judgment. Other signs can include driving much too fast or too slowly, sudden stops, and jerky movements, but proper signaling is not a sign of impairment.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When turning left, to whom must you yield?
options: a:Only to vehicles that have a green arrow.,b:Oncoming traffic and any pedestrians in the intersection.,c:Only to the driver on your right.
note: When turning left, you must yield to oncoming traffic that is close enough to be a hazard and to pedestrians and bicyclists crossing your path. They have the right‑of‑way until it is clearly safe for you to complete the turn.

question: At a railroad crossing, how far must you stop from the nearest rail when warning lights are flashing?
options: a:Can drive around a lowered gate if no train is coming.,b:Must stop at least 15 feet from the nearest rail when warning lights are flashing.,c:Must stop at least 10 feet from the nearest rail.
note: When the lights are flashing or gates are down at a railroad crossing, you must stop at least 15 feet and no more than 50 feet from the nearest rail. Stopping well back gives room for the train to pass safely and for any overhanging parts of the train. Never drive around lowered gates, even if you do not see a train.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When is it illegal to drive below the posted speed limit?
options: a:Only in heavy traffic in a construction zone.,b:When driving so slowly that you disrupt the normal flow of traffic.,c:Only in rural areas.
note: You must not drive so slowly that you block or disrupt the normal flow of traffic, unless it is necessary for safety or required by law. If your slow speed is holding up traffic, you may be required to pull over and let other vehicles pass.

question: What is defensive driving?
options: a:Identifying hazardous situations and acting to avoid accidents.,b:Getting ahead of other drivers to avoid problems.,c:Following the vehicle ahead closely to observe its actions.
note: Defensive driving means constantly scanning for potential hazards and adjusting your speed, position, and actions early to prevent collisions. You focus on space, visibility, and time so you can react safely before a situation becomes dangerous.

question: When should you increase your following distance?
options: a:When conditions reduce visibility or make it harder to stop, such as following a large vehicle that blocks your view.,b:Only when exiting an expressway.,c:Only when following a motorcycle.
note: You should increase your following distance whenever conditions make it harder to see, stop, or maneuver—such as when following large vehicles that block your view, in bad weather, at higher speeds, in heavy traffic, when being tailgated, or when following motorcycles or other vulnerable road users.

question: If another vehicle is about to hit you, what is an appropriate immediate action?
options: a:Sound your horn and be ready to brake or steer to reduce or avoid the collision.,b:Wave your arms frantically.,c:Only use emergency lights.
note: If a collision seems likely, using your horn is one of the quickest ways to warn another driver who may not see you. You should also be prepared to brake, steer, or accelerate to reduce the impact or avoid the crash, but sounding the horn is an appropriate immediate action to get their attention.

question: Drivers may not pass from either side of which centerline?
options: a:Single broken yellow,b:Combination broken and solid yellow,c:Double solid yellow
note: A double solid yellow centerline means traffic in both directions is prohibited from crossing the line to pass. You may cross it only when turning left into or out of a driveway or side road when it is safe, but not for passing other vehicles.

question: Which of these is a common cause of distracted driving?
options: a:Changing a radio station or media device.,b:Eating while driving.,c:Talking or texting on a cellular phone, as well as other tasks that take your attention from the road.
note: Talking or texting on a cell phone is one of the most dangerous and common forms of distracted driving because it takes your eyes, hands, and mind away from driving. Other activities like changing the radio or eating are also distractions and should be minimized so you can keep full attention on the road.

question: What color are signs that indicate areas of public recreation or historic sites?
options: a:Brown.,b:Green.,c:Orange.
note: Brown traffic signs are used to indicate public recreation areas, parks, cultural points of interest, and historic sites so drivers can easily identify locations for leisure and tourism.

question: Which of these effects does alcohol NOT cause?
options: a:It distorts judgment of speed and distance.,b:It makes you more alert.,c:It slows reflexes and reaction time.
note: Alcohol is a depressant. It slows reflexes and reaction time, reduces alertness, and distorts your judgment of speed, distance, and risk. It does not make you more alert; instead, it makes safe driving much more difficult.

question: At a light rail crossing, what must drivers always do?
options: a:Obey traffic signals and look both ways before crossing tracks.,b:Drive around lowered crossing gates if safe.,c:Assume trains will yield to vehicles.
note: At any rail or light rail crossing, you must always obey all warning signs, signals, and gates, and look carefully both ways down the tracks before crossing. Never drive around lowered gates and never assume a train will stop for you.

question: Why is extra alertness required around motorcycles?
options: a:They are smaller and harder to see, often hidden in blind spots.,b:They rarely use lights at night.,c:Motorcyclists are generally less skilled than car drivers.
note: Motorcycles are small and can be easily hidden in blind spots or masked by other traffic, making them harder to see and judge for speed and distance. Drivers must check mirrors and blind spots carefully and use extra caution when turning or changing lanes near motorcycles.

question: What is the purpose of highway pavement markings?
options: a:Are only found in construction zones.,b:Provide information and guide drivers.,c:Are usually not important.
note: Highway pavement markings guide and regulate traffic. They show lane boundaries, where passing is allowed, turn lanes, crosswalks, and other important information so drivers can position their vehicles correctly and drive safely.

question: Why should you exercise extra caution when near snowplows?
options: a:They usually drive faster than other vehicles.,b:They are typically narrower than most vehicles.,c:They often reduce visibility by creating clouds of blowing snow.
note: Snowplows are large, slow-moving vehicles that often throw snow, slush, and ice into the air, creating clouds that can severely reduce visibility. They may also be wider than a normal lane because of their plow blades. You should slow down, stay well back, and give them extra room to operate safely.

question: What should you do when the road is slippery from rain, snow, or ice?
options: a:Drive at the posted speed limit regardless of conditions.,b:Slow down and drive more cautiously than normal.,c:Use cruise control to maintain a steady speed.
note: On wet, snowy, or icy roads, traction is reduced and it is easier to lose control. You should slow down, increase your following distance, and make all steering, braking, and accelerating movements gently. Avoid cruise control so you can respond quickly to changes in traction.

question: If an emergency vehicle with flashing lights is nearby, what should you do?
options: a:Stop your vehicle immediately and prevent them from passing.,b:Make every effort to give the emergency vehicle a clear path of travel.,c:Speed up to avoid the emergency vehicle.
note: Yield the right-of-way: move to the side and stop if necessary so the emergency vehicle can pass safely.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: If you miss your exit on an interstate expressway, what should you do?
options: a:Stop and make a U-turn.,b:Roll down your window and ask the driver next to you for help.,c:Get off at the next exit and come back to the exit you missed.
note: If you miss your exit on a freeway or interstate, continue to the next exit. Then re-enter the highway going the opposite direction if needed and return to the exit you missed. Never stop, back up, or make a U‑turn on the highway, as this is extremely dangerous and usually illegal.

question: At night, when another vehicle is approaching from the opposite direction, your headlights should be:
options: a:Off — use parking lights instead.,b:Set to high beam.,c:Set to low beam.
note: When another vehicle is approaching at night, you must use low‑beam headlights so you do not blind the oncoming driver. High beams can cause glare and make it hard for the other driver to see the road. Switch to low beams within about 500 feet of an oncoming vehicle (distance may vary slightly by state).

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: If you are on a divided multilane highway and hear or see an approaching emergency vehicle, what should you do?
options: a:Continue at the same speed and let it pass.,b:Slow down and, if safe, move over and stop to yield a clear path.,c:Disregard the signal if other lanes are open.
note: On a divided multilane highway, you must still yield to an approaching emergency vehicle using lights or siren. Safely move to the nearest edge of your lane, slow down, and stop if necessary to provide a clear path. Do not just continue at the same speed or ignore the signal, even if there are other open lanes.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: At a four-way intersection controlled by stop signs, if two drivers arrive at the same time, who has the right-of-way?
options: a:The driver who signals first.,b:The driver on the left.,c:The driver on the right.
note: At a four-way stop, if two vehicles arrive at the same time, the driver on the left must yield to the driver on the right. This helps avoid confusion and keeps traffic moving safely through the intersection.

question: Which of the following statements is NOT true?
options: a:Wearing a safety belt helps a driver maintain control of their vehicle.,b:A child safety seat should never be placed in front of an active airbag.,c:Only persons under the age of 18 are required to wear a seat belt.
note: Wearing a safety belt helps keep you behind the wheel and in control during sudden stops or crashes, and a child safety seat should never be placed in front of an active airbag because the airbag can seriously injure a child. In Vermont, as in many states, all occupants must be properly restrained, so the statement that only persons under 18 are required to wear a seat belt is not true.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When you approach an intersection with a flashing red light, what must you do?
options: a:Come to a full stop and go when it is safe to do so.,b:Stop only if other cars are already within the intersection.,c:Stop only if other cars are also approaching the intersection.
note: A flashing red light means the same as a stop sign. You must come to a complete stop, check for traffic and pedestrians, yield the right-of-way as needed, and then proceed only when it is safe. You do not stop only when other vehicles are present; the stop is always required.

question: Before entering a roundabout, to whom must you yield?
options: a:Only large vehicles inside the roundabout.,b:All traffic already in the roundabout and pedestrians in crosswalks.,c:Only pedestrians.
note: Before entering a roundabout, you must yield to all traffic already in the circle, including cars, trucks, motorcycles, and bicycles, as well as to pedestrians in crosswalks at the entrances and exits. Wait for a safe gap before entering.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: If a driver's left arm is extended downward, what does that hand signal indicate?
options: a:Stop.,b:Turn left.,c:Turn right.
note: A driver’s left arm extended downward with the palm facing to the rear is the standard hand signal for slowing or stopping. When you see this signal from a vehicle ahead, be prepared to slow down and stop because their brake lights may be hard to see or not working.

question: How should you drive when passing through a work zone?
options: a:Keep a two-second following distance behind any vehicle ahead of you.,b:Slow down and pay attention.,c:Closely follow the vehicle ahead to clear the zone quickly.
note: In work zones you must slow down, watch for workers, equipment, and changing traffic patterns, and maintain a larger following distance than usual. Avoid sudden lane changes and be prepared to stop unexpectedly.

question: How can stress affect your driving?
options: a:Decreasing your chances of an accident.,b:Causing you to fall asleep at the wheel.,c:Lowering your ability to focus on driving.
note: Stress and strong emotions can distract you, narrow your attention, and slow your reaction time. This lowers your ability to focus on driving and increases your risk of making poor decisions or missing hazards, so it’s safer not to drive when you are very upset or stressed.

question: What does a green traffic arrow mean when displayed for a lane?
options: a:It allows you to proceed in any direction.,b:It is used only on one-way streets.,c:It functions like a circular green light
note: A green arrow means you may proceed only in the direction the arrow points, and you generally have the right‑of‑way for that movement if the intersection is clear. It does not allow you to go in any direction you choose, and it is not limited to one‑way streets.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: What does a solid yellow arrow at a traffic signal mean?
options: a:It means drivers may turn in the arrow direction without yielding.,b:It is never used.,c:It has the same meaning as a circular yellow light — slow and prepare to stop.
note: A solid yellow arrow means the protected turn phase is ending and a red arrow is about to appear. You should slow down and prepare to stop; complete the turn only if you are already in the intersection and it would be unsafe to stop suddenly.

question: What does a slow-moving vehicle emblem look like?
options: a:A rectangular red sign.,b:A diamond-shaped yellow sign.,c:A reflective orange triangle.
note: The slow-moving vehicle emblem is a reflective orange triangle with a red border. It is mounted on the rear of vehicles that typically travel 25 mph or less, warning faster traffic to use extra caution and be prepared to slow down.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: What does a posted speed limit indicate?
options: a:The maximum legal speed under ideal road and weather conditions.,b:The exact safe speed you must always drive to avoid a ticket.,c:Only a suggested speed.
note: A posted speed limit is the maximum legal speed allowed on that road in ideal conditions. You must slow down below the limit when conditions are poor—such as rain, fog, heavy traffic, or bad road surfaces—to drive at a speed that is safe and reasonable.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When on a narrow road and meeting an oncoming vehicle, what should you allow?
options: a:Demand the other vehicle pull over to make room.,b:Allow the oncoming vehicle at least one-half of the main-traveled portion of the road.,c:Pull completely off the road and stop.
note: On a narrow road, each driver must share the roadway so both vehicles can pass safely. You should allow the oncoming vehicle at least one-half of the main-traveled portion of the road and adjust your position and speed so there is safe clearance between vehicles. You are not required to pull completely off the road unless it is necessary for safety.

question: In which situations is it important to slow down?
options: a:At intersections or railroad crossings.,b:When the road is wet or slippery.,c:On narrow or winding roads.
note: You must slow down whenever conditions require extra caution, including at intersections and railroad crossings, on narrow or winding roads, on hills and sharp curves, and when the road is wet or slippery. The safest approach is to reduce speed in all of these situations so you have more time to react.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When two vehicles enter an intersection at the same time from different highways, which driver must yield?
options: a:The driver on the left must yield to the driver on the right.,b:Either driver depending on who signals first.,c:The driver on the right must yield to the left.
note: At an uncontrolled intersection where two vehicles arrive at the same time from different roads, the driver on the left must yield to the driver on the right. This right-of-way rule helps prevent confusion and collisions when there are no signs or signals.

question: In bad weather, what should drivers do about following distance?
options: a:Decrease their following distance.,b:Increase their following distance.,c:Increase their speed to reach their destination faster.
note: In rain, snow, fog, or on icy roads, your stopping distance increases and it is harder to see hazards. You should leave more space between your vehicle and the one ahead so you have extra time and distance to brake smoothly and avoid collisions.

question: Which of these is an effect of alcohol on drivers?
options: a:Loss of concentration.,b:Poor coordination.,c:Slower judgment.
note: Alcohol affects many parts of your driving ability at the same time. It reduces concentration, slows and distorts judgment, and harms coordination and reaction time. Any of the listed effects can occur even at relatively low blood alcohol levels, which is why you should never drive after drinking.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: If a traffic signal shows a red light and a green arrow at the same time, what does it allow?
options: a:You must wait for a solid green light before proceeding in any direction.,b:You may proceed only in the direction indicated by the green arrow.,c:You may proceed only straight ahead.
note: A red light means you must stop and may not go straight or turn in directions not indicated. A green arrow means you are allowed to proceed only in the direction of the arrow, after yielding to pedestrians and other traffic that still has the right‑of‑way. When both are shown together, you may go only in the arrow’s direction if the way is clear.

question: If you are upset, nervous, or crying, how should you handle driving?
options: a:You will drive no differently than you would if you were calm.,b:Take the time to calm and focus before starting the engine.,c:You can drive faster because you are more alert.
note: Strong emotions like anger, fear, or sadness distract you from the road and slow your reactions. If you are very upset or crying, wait until you have calmed down and can focus fully before starting to drive so you can make safe decisions and respond quickly to traffic conditions.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When is it lawful to pass another vehicle on the right?
options: a:On a narrow bridge.,b:Even if it requires driving off the pavement.,c:When the other vehicle is waiting or turning left and there is a safe available lane on the right.
note: You may pass on the right only when it can be done safely and without leaving the paved roadway, such as on multi‑lane roads or when the vehicle ahead is turning left and there is a clear lane to the right. It is illegal and dangerous to pass on the right by driving off the pavement or on narrow bridges.

question: When is it necessary to look over your shoulder to check a blind spot?
options: a:Only when preparing to park.,b:Only when turning right.,c:When changing lanes or otherwise moving your vehicle laterally (e.g., merging or pulling toward/away from a curb).
note: You must briefly look over your shoulder to check your blind spot any time you move your vehicle sideways into an area you cannot see with your mirrors alone. This includes changing lanes, merging, and pulling toward or away from a curb, because vehicles, motorcycles, or bicycles can be hidden in these blind spots.

question: When driving in fog, which lights should you use?
options: a:High beam headlights.,b:Parking lights only.,c:Low beam headlights (and fog lights if equipped).
note: Use low beam headlights in fog because their light aims down toward the road and reduces glare. High beams reflect off the water droplets in fog and can bounce back into your eyes, making it harder to see. If your vehicle has fog lights, use them with your low beams for better visibility.

question: Before changing lanes, what should you make sure to do?
options: a:Only rely on your mirrors.,b:Check side and rearview mirrors, signal, and glance over your shoulder for blind spots.,c:Only check for oncoming traffic ahead.
note: Before changing lanes, check your mirrors to see traffic behind and beside you, signal early to let others know your intentions, and quickly glance over your shoulder to check your blind spot. This combination helps ensure the lane is clear and reduces the risk of sideswipe collisions.

question: Which commonly causes traffic accidents?
options: a:Inattentive driving and excessive speed for conditions as well as following too closely.,b:Only bad weather.,c:Mechanical failures exclusively.
note: Many crashes are caused by driver behavior such as not paying attention, driving too fast for road or weather conditions, and following other vehicles too closely. These behaviors reduce the time and space you have to react to hazards, greatly increasing the chance of a collision.

question: How serious is drinking alcohol and then driving?
options: a:Acceptable after only a couple of drinks.,b:A minor issue if you feel sober.,c:A serious traffic safety problem because alcohol impairs the skills needed for safe driving.
note: Drinking and driving is a serious safety problem because alcohol slows your reaction time, reduces coordination, and impairs judgment, even at low levels. Any amount of alcohol can make driving unsafe, and driving while impaired is illegal and greatly increases your risk of a crash.

question: How should a seat belt fit when adjusted properly?
options: a:Is buckled snugly across your hip bones and lower abdomen.,b:Is hidden beneath the seat.,c:Is loose.
note: A properly adjusted lap belt should be buckled snugly across your hip bones and lower abdomen, not loose. The shoulder belt should cross the center of your chest and shoulder, never under your arm or behind your back. A snug fit keeps your body in place so the belt can absorb crash forces and prevent serious injury.

question: When must drivers yield to pedestrians?
options: a:Always when pedestrians are in the street, even if they cross carelessly.,b:Only if the pedestrian is using a crosswalk.,c:Only if they are on the same side of the street as the driver.
note: Drivers must always yield to pedestrians who are in the roadway, whether they are in a marked crosswalk, an unmarked crosswalk at an intersection, or crossing elsewhere. Even if a pedestrian is crossing carelessly or illegally, you are required to use caution, slow down, and yield to avoid hitting them.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: Is signaling before turning, changing lanes, or pulling away from a curb mandatory?
options: a:You need only signal during the maneuver itself.,b:Yes — signaling is required by law and is a good driving habit.,c:No — signal only if other traffic is present.
note: You must signal at least 100 feet before turning or changing lanes; always signal before pulling away from a curb.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: What must a driver do when approaching a flashing red traffic signal?
options: a:Slow down at the light.,b:Stop,c:Merge to the right.
note: A flashing red traffic signal means you must come to a complete stop, just as you would at a stop sign. After stopping, yield to any pedestrians and other vehicles already in or close to the intersection, and proceed only when it is safe and the way is clear.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When you hear or see an emergency vehicle approaching, what should you do?
options: a:Proceed slowly and ignore it if possible.,b:Stop immediately in your current lane.,c:Drive as far right as is safe and stop.
note: When an emergency vehicle with flashing lights and siren approaches, you must yield the right-of-way by pulling as far to the right side of the road as is safe and stopping until it has passed. Do not stop in the middle of a lane or in an intersection, and never try to outrun or follow closely behind an emergency vehicle.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: To enter a freeway, you should:
options: a:Signal, yield to existing traffic, and enter at the same speed that traffic is moving.,b:Signal and enter; freeway traffic must yield to you.,c:Drive slowly on the entrance ramp so you can check traffic.
note: On a freeway entrance ramp, use the acceleration lane to build up speed, signal early, and merge only when there is a safe gap. You must yield to traffic already on the freeway and adjust your speed so you enter at or near the flow of traffic, not much slower or faster.

question: If you become stranded in a snowstorm, what is the best course of action?
options: a:Stay in your car and wait for help.,b:Get out and walk for help immediately.,c:Lie down and sleep in the car.
note: In a snowstorm, it is usually safest to stay in your vehicle. Your car offers shelter, makes you easier to find, and protects you from getting lost or exposed to extreme cold. Run the engine only periodically for heat, keep a window slightly open for fresh air, and make sure the exhaust pipe is clear of snow.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: What does a red arrow signal require you to do?
options: a:Stop and remain stopped until the signal changes to a green light or green arrow.,b:Slow down and proceed if the way looks clear.,c:Creep forward into the intersection and wait.
note: A red arrow means you must come to a complete stop and stay stopped in the direction of that arrow. You may not turn in the direction of the arrow until it changes to green or a green arrow, and you must obey any posted signs about turns on red.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: By law, how far before a turn or lane change must you signal?
options: a:100 feet or about three to five seconds in normal driving.,b:10 feet,before turning.,c:50 feet before the turn.,d:30 feet before the turn.
note: You must signal at least 100 feet before a turn or lane change; signaling three to five seconds in advance is a good rule.

question: When you enter a car to drive, what should you adjust first?
options: a:Your seat so you can reach the controls and see the road clearly.,b:The steering wheel, then the seat.,c:Only your rearview mirror.
note: Before driving, adjust your seat first so you can reach the pedals and controls comfortably and see clearly over the dashboard. Once your seating position is correct, then adjust mirrors and the steering wheel to match that position.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When must you yield the right-of-way to an emergency vehicle?
options: a:Under no circumstances.,b:Only when other vehicles yield,c:When you see flashing lights or hear a siren.
note: You must always yield to emergency vehicles using a siren and/or flashing lights. Safely pull to the right edge of the road and stop, if possible, so they have a clear path. Remain stopped until the emergency vehicle has passed, unless directed otherwise by law enforcement.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When passing on a two-way road, when should you return to your lane?
options: a:Only after signaling for at least five seconds.,b:Immediately after passing the vehicle's rear bumper.,c:When there is enough room between you and the vehicle you passed and you can see it in your rearview mirror.
note: When passing on a two‑way road, you should not return to your lane until you can see the front of the vehicle you passed in your rearview mirror and there is a safe distance between your vehicle and the one you passed. Always signal before returning and make sure you are fully clear without cutting back in too closely.

question: If you experience a tire blowout while driving, what should you do?
options: a:Take your foot off the gas and brake hard to stop quickly.,b:Do not immediately use your brakes; gradually slow down and pull off the road.,c:Immediately steer to the side of the road, even if you must brake hard.
note: If a tire blows out, hold the steering wheel firmly and keep the vehicle going straight. Ease your foot off the gas and let the car slow down gradually. Do not slam on the brakes, because that can cause loss of control. When the vehicle has slowed and you are in control, gently brake as needed and steer to the side of the road to stop in a safe place.

question: If you notice a defect that may affect safe operation of your vehicle, what should you do?
options: a:Correct the defect as soon as possible.,b:Drive the vehicle at slower speeds until you can get it fixed.,c:Correct the defect when you can afford it.
note: Any defect that could affect the safe operation of your vehicle—such as problems with brakes, tires, steering, or lights—should be repaired as soon as possible. Driving with known safety defects increases the risk of a crash and may be illegal. Do not rely on simply driving slower; fix the problem before using the vehicle normally.

question: What are the rights and responsibilities of bicyclists on most roads?
options: a:They may not ride on public roads.,b:They have fewer rules to follow than motorists.,c:They have the same rights and responsibilities as motor vehicle operators.
note: On most public roads, bicyclists have the same rights and responsibilities as drivers of motor vehicles. They must obey traffic signals and signs, ride in the same direction as traffic, and signal turns and stops. Motorists must treat bicycles as legitimate road users and give them safe space when passing.

question: What effect does alcohol have on driving skills?
options: a:It slows reflexes and reaction times.,b:It makes you more alert.,c:It improves concentration.
note: Alcohol is a depressant that slows your brain and nervous system. This reduces your reaction time, coordination, and judgment, all of which are critical for safe driving. Even small amounts of alcohol can make you slower to respond to hazards and less able to make good decisions behind the wheel.

question: If an emergency vehicle is directly behind you in heavy traffic, what should you do?
options: a:Stop where you are.,b:Keep moving slowly until you can safely pull over to the right and stop.,c:Speed up to get out of the way.
note: When an emergency vehicle approaches from behind with lights and siren on, you must yield the right‑of‑way. In heavy traffic, do not stop in the lane and do not speed up. Instead, continue moving slowly and carefully until you can safely pull as far to the right as possible and stop, allowing the emergency vehicle a clear path.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: What must you do when entering a roadway from a private road or driveway?
options: a:Stop with part of your car on the roadway to alert others.,b:Yield the right-of-way to pedestrians and vehicles already on the roadway.,c:Drive out quickly to merge with traffic.
note: When entering a public road from a private road, driveway, or alley, you must yield to all pedestrians on the sidewalk and to all vehicles already traveling on the roadway. Do not pull out quickly or stop with part of your vehicle in the traffic lane; wait until the way is clear and then enter safely.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: If two vehicles arrive at an uncontrolled intersection at the same time, which vehicle must yield?
options: a:The vehicle on the right must yield to the vehicle on the left.,b:The vehicle on the left must yield to the vehicle on the right.,c:The largest vehicle has the right‑of‑way.
note: At an uncontrolled intersection (no signs or signals), if two vehicles arrive at the same time, the driver on the left must yield to the driver on the right. This rule helps prevent confusion and collisions by clearly assigning who goes first when there is no traffic control device.

question: To reduce headlight glare from oncoming vehicles at night, where should you look?
options: a:Straight ahead.,b:At the right side of the road or lane edge ahead.,c:Over the shoulder.
note: To reduce glare from oncoming headlights at night, avoid looking directly into the lights. Instead, glance toward the right side of your lane and use the road’s right edge or lane markings as a guide. This keeps you oriented in your lane while minimizing the temporary blindness caused by bright headlights.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When parked uphill next to a curb, how should you turn your steering wheel?
options: a:Keep the front tires straight ahead and release the parking brake.,b:Turn the rear tires against the curb.,c:Turn your front wheels away from the curb and set the parking brake.
note: When you park facing uphill next to a curb, turn your front wheels away from the curb and set the parking brake. If the vehicle starts to roll, the back of the front tire will move into the curb and stop the car from rolling into traffic.

question: In most fatal crashes involving a large truck and a passenger vehicle, who is responsible for causing the crash?
options: a:Poor weather.,b:The driver of the passenger vehicle.,c:The truck driver.
note: Crash studies show that in most fatal collisions involving a large truck and a passenger vehicle, the driver of the passenger vehicle is found to have caused the crash. This is often due to unsafe maneuvers around trucks, such as cutting in too closely, driving in blind spots, or misjudging stopping distances.

question: If your car breaks down on a highway, what should you do first?
options: a:Stay seated and wait for help without turning on hazards.,b:Sound your horn to alert passing drivers.,c:Signal and carefully exit the roadway
note: If your car breaks down on a highway, your first priority is to get out of the flow of traffic. Signal, move to the shoulder or as far off the roadway as safely possible, then turn on your hazard lights and raise the hood to show your vehicle is disabled.

question: How does smoking or preparing to smoke while driving affect your driving?
options: a:Helps maintain driver alertness.,b:Do not affect driving abilities.,c:Are distracting activities.
note: Smoking or preparing to smoke while driving is a distraction. It takes at least one hand off the wheel and can draw your eyes and attention away from the road, especially if you drop something hot like ashes or a cigarette. Any activity that diverts your attention, hands, or eyes from driving increases your crash risk.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: Which of these has priority if there is a conflict: a steady red light, a police officer, or a stop sign?
options: a:A steady red light,b:A police officer,c:A stop sign
note: An authorized police officer or traffic officer directing traffic always has priority over traffic lights, signs, and pavement markings. If an officer’s directions conflict with a red light or stop sign, you must follow the officer’s instructions.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: To check your blind spot when moving left, where should you glance?
options: a:Only at the side mirror.,b:Over your right shoulder.,c:Over your left shoulder.
note: When moving left, you must check the blind spot on your left side by quickly glancing over your left shoulder. Mirrors alone cannot show this area, so a shoulder check in the direction you intend to move is essential before changing lanes or merging.

question: Compared to smaller vehicles, larger vehicles have:
options: a:No blind spots.,b:Smaller blind spots.,c:Larger blind spots.
note: Large vehicles such as trucks and buses have larger blind spots than smaller vehicles. These areas are directly behind, along both sides, and sometimes in front of the vehicle where the driver cannot see you in the mirrors. Avoid driving for long periods in these blind spots so the driver can see you and react safely.

question: Which driving technique helps avoid crashes on snowy or icy roads?
options: a:Engage four‑wheel drive and maintain normal speeds.,b:Add extra weight to the vehicle to improve traction.,c:Reduce your speed and increase your following distance.
note: On snowy or icy roads, the most important safety steps are to slow down and leave more space between you and the vehicle ahead. Reduced speed gives you more time to react, and a greater following distance allows for the much longer stopping distances needed on slippery surfaces.

question: What is true about drivers who have consumed alcohol before driving?
options: a:They are better drivers because they are more cautious.,b:They are always aware of the risks they are taking.,c:They do not have sufficient control over their bodies.
note: Any amount of alcohol can reduce your control over your body and your driving. It slows reaction time, affects coordination, and impairs judgment and vision, making it harder to steer, brake, and respond to hazards. Because of this loss of control, you should never drive after drinking.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
